increments.title: A Frontend user whose address is not already saved reaches a dead end on every address-selection page; Design release 1 offers a route to add a new address on all of them and returns the user with the new address chosen
increments.detail:
On any of Frontend's five consignment party pickers, a search that matches nothing renders one line — "No addresses match your search." — and nothing else: no link, no button, no guidance (fe-address-picker-place-of-origin-no-matches). The only control left is "Save and continue", and submitting without a row selected returns "Select a consignor from the list" in an error summary (fe-address-picker-consignor-or-exporter-error), so the page cannot be satisfied at all. The picker form is a search input, a Search button, the results table, its pagination and Save and continue, and nothing more (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/party-picker/_address-picker.njk:69-113); the addresses feature's copy holds no add-an-address key at all, the empty state's only string being noMatches (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/copy/copy.en.js:43-62). The contact-address page is a different shape — the whole book as thirteen radios rather than a search — but it is the same dead end: it offers no way to add an address either (fe-contact). Searching the rendered DOM of every one of the 31 captured Frontend screens and 36 captured states for "add a new address", "add an address" or "address book" returns nothing. So a trader whose place of origin has never been saved cannot finish the addresses section, and the service gives them no way to find that out except by failing.

Design release 1 gives every address-selection page a route out to add one. On the five party pickers it is a secondary "Add a new address" button sitting under the results table and above "Save and continue" — six captured screens carry it, the five picker headings plus the search-filtered state — pointing at /address-book/add?from=<section> (app/views/consignment-address-select.html:162-163, with the href built at app/routes.js:3598-3600). On the contact-address page it is worded differently and sits above the radios, as a link inside the sentence "If the correct address is not shown, add a new branch address, then return to this page.", pointing at /address-book/add?from=contact-address. Following either skips the address-type chooser, because the section the user came from implies the type and is carried in a hidden addressType, and lands on "Add address details" (dr1-address-book-add-from-party-picker), where the address can be searched for or typed in by hand. Saving writes the address to the book, selects it into the section the user came from, redirects them back to that same page and shows a success message naming the address just added (app/routes.js:8118-8194). The notification is never abandoned.

Give every address-selection page a route out, and a return path back to it with the new address selected — the five pickers and the contact-address page. Nothing has to land first: the address-book API behind Frontend already serves create, and every other part of the picker exists. What a person has to choose is the destination, and it is the same choice this run's scope question turns on (address-book--saved-address-book-pages-absent) — either an add-address page inside this frontend, which means giving its address-book service a write path it deliberately does not have (src/server/app/services/address-book/index.js:17-19), or a link out to the Import Notification Service front door's existing /address-book/add, which needs a return URL so the user comes back to the page they left rather than being stranded in another service's address book. The empty state's copy is part of the work either way: "No addresses match your search." is a statement with no next step in it.

FALSIFIED BY: Finding any link or button on a Frontend party picker or the contact-address page that leads to adding an address.

finding.correction: The author wrote that Design release 1 "puts a secondary 'Add a new address' button under the results table on all five party pickers and on the contact-address page — seven captured screens carry it". The button claim is right for the pickers and wrong for the contact-address page. Grepping the prototype capture for "Add a new address" returns eight files: the six consignment-address-select screens (the five picker headings plus the search-filtered state), dr1-address-book.html, where it is the list page's own primary button, and dr1-address-book-add.html, where it is a caption above the heading rather than a button at all. dr1-contact-address-for-consignment.html is not among them: it carries the link "add a new branch address" at line 269 of the captured DOM, inside a sentence above the radios, and the screenshot shows it as body copy rather than a button. The underlying claim — that Design release 1 offers a route to add an address where Frontend offers none — holds on that page too, and the href is the same /address-book/add?from= shape, so the slot has been corrected rather than narrowed: the count is now six picker screens, the contact page's own wording and placement are stated, and fe-contact and dr1-contact-address-for-consignment have been added to screens with "add a new branch address" added to controls so that page's card crops its own control. The title was widened from "every picker" to "every address-selection page" to match. The falsifier's second sentence, which asserted the picker DOM carries only five things, has been dropped: the error state also carries an error summary, and the first sentence is the falsifier. Note for the cross-slice sweep: fe-contact, dr1-contact-address-for-consignment and dr1-consignment-address-select belong to the addresses slice in slices.json, so this finding reaches across the boundary by design — the address-book slice note licenses it, but a duplicate from the addresses author is possible.

Opened fe-address-picker-place-of-origin-no-matches.png, dr1-consignment-address-select.png and dr1-contact-address-for-consignment.png. Checked rubric 1 rather than taking the dead end on the page's word: fe-address-picker-consignor-or-exporter-error.html carries "There is a problem" and "Select a consignor from the list" both in the error summary and inline, so the picker is mandatory and the claim is about the journey, not only the markup — it stands. Checked both DR1 citations at the cited lines: app/views/consignment-address-select.html:161-165 is the govukButton and app/routes.js:3598-3600 is the addAddressHref ternary, both root-mount, and read saveAddressBookEntry at app/routes.js:8118-8194 to confirm the write, the section sync, the success message and the redirect back to consignmentReturn.path. Confirmed "Add a new address" appears exactly once on dr1-consignment-address-select.html, so the crop resolves. Rubric 2 fired on the prototype slot — see correction.

relatedTo.why: Where the button leads depends on whether Design release 1's eight address-book pages are this frontend's work; the button itself is needed either way.

citations.why: The claim is that the secondary Add a new address button sits under the results table and above Save and continue. The cited 162-163 held only the button text and href, so the ordering the sentence describes was not in the range. 161-170 covers both buttons in document order: the table and fieldset close at 157-158, the Add a new address button is 161-165 with href addAddressHref, and Save and continue follows at 167-170.

increments.title: A Frontend trader who spots a wrong saved address on a party picker can only read it; Design release 1 links every row to the saved record, where it can be edited or deleted before the trader is returned to the picker
increments.detail:
On a Frontend party picker each row's "View details" is a disclosure that opens in place (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/party-picker/_address-picker.njk:28-41), revealing the saved record as a plain list built from name, address lines, country, telephone number and email address (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/party-picker/view-model/address-lines.js:15-22). The captured place-of-origin picker carries five of them, and the first opens to seven lines for Astra Rosales ending "01632 960000" and "astra-rosales@example.com". The row offers nothing else: no Edit, no Delete, no link out. So a trader who sees that a saved consignor has moved, that a postcode is wrong, or that the same farm is in the book twice, has no way to correct or remove it anywhere in this service, and the only thing they can do is pick the wrong record or abandon the section. Searching the rendered DOM of all 31 captured Frontend screens and 36 captured states for "edit address", "change this address", "edit this address" and "delete address" returns nothing. This is deliberate in the code: the address-book service exposes only search, all and party, and says "This service reads and never writes. The notification journey selects from the organisation's book; adding, changing and removing the records in it belongs to the INS frontend, which is the only writer" (src/server/app/services/address-book/index.js:17-19). The transporter list is the same shape, its rows leading nowhere either.

In Design release 1 the same "View details" is a link out of the row to the saved address's own page, carrying the page the trader came from in a return parameter, so a row on the place-of-origin picker points at /address-book/<id>?return=%2Fplace-of-origin (app/views/consignment-address-select.html:152, with the href built at app/routes.js:3562). That page is dr1-address-book-view: the record's name as the heading, a summary list of eight facts, and then an "Edit" button beside a red "Delete" button. Edit opens dr1-address-book-edit, headed "Edit address and contact details", with all nine address and contact fields prefilled and already open, the address search suppressed, and "Save changes" beside "Cancel"; the return parameter is carried into the form action, so saving or cancelling puts the trader back on the picker they left rather than stranding them in the address book, and the delete honours the same parameter. Design release 1's transporter list links its rows to the same record page. So in Design release 1 a wrong saved address is fixed where it is noticed, and the notification is never abandoned.

Give every picker row a route to the saved record and a way back to the page the trader left. This is the maintenance half of the route the add finding covers, and it turns on the same choice of destination: either an address record page inside this frontend, which means giving its address-book service the update and delete it deliberately does not have (src/server/app/services/address-book/index.js:17-19), or a link into the Import Notification Service front door's existing address-book record and edit pages, which needs a return URL so the trader comes back to the picker. The address-book API already serves update and delete, so nothing has to land first either way and the band is frontend-work. Raise it separately from the add route because it is a different control, a different user need -- correcting or removing a record rather than creating one -- and because it was until now carried by nobody: the addresses slice recorded both "View details" behaviours and passed the question to address-book--saved-address-book-pages-absent, and the transport slice left Design release 1's transporter "View details" link out for the same reason, but neither that finding nor the add-route finding asks for the route. Whether the in-place disclosure survives alongside the link is a design call for whoever does the work; Design release 1 shows only the link. The named control, "View details", occurs five times on the Frontend picker and nine times on the Design release 1 one, so both cards will be refused a crop and fall back to the whole page with the reason printed. That is the right picture here: the finding is about what a row leads to, not about one row.

FALSIFIED BY: Finding any control on a Frontend party picker, transporter list or contact-address page that leads to changing or removing a saved address-book record.

increments.title: Design release 1 gives a trader a saved address book they can search, filter by type, add to, view, edit and delete; Frontend has no address-book page and its journey can only read the book
increments.detail:
Frontend has no address book as a page. Its service navigation carries no items, so nothing links to a saved-addresses page, and searching the rendered DOM of all 31 captured Frontend screens and 36 captured states for "address book" or "add a new address" returns nothing. A trader meets the organisation's book only inside the five consignment party pickers and the contact-address page, and there only as a read-only chooser: the pickers offer a Search input hinted "Name, address or country", a secondary Search button, a five-row results table with a radio per row and a "View details" expander, pagination, and "Save and continue" (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/party-picker/_address-picker.njk:69-113), and the contact-address page offers the whole book as one radio list. Nothing anywhere adds, changes or removes a record. Frontend's address-book service exposes only search, all and party, and states the split as a design decision: "This service reads and never writes. The notification journey selects from the organisation's book; adding, changing and removing the records in it belongs to the INS frontend, which is the only writer" (src/server/app/services/address-book/index.js:17-19). Frontend's records also carry no address type at all, deliberately, because the same record may be a consignor on one notification and a consignee on the next (src/server/app/services/address-book/index.js:12-15).

Design release 1 gives the trader an address book of their own, reached from a service-navigation item on every page, and eight captured screens describe it. dr1-address-book is the list: heading "Address book", intro "Manage your addresses for use across import notifications.", a primary "Add a new address" button, a "Filter addresses" panel holding a Search box placeholdered "Search by name, address or country" and a "Type" select offering Place of Origin, Consignor, Consignee, Importer, Place of Destination, Transporter and Branch Address, a result count ("Showing 1-8 of 58"), a Name / Type / Address / Country table with a "View" link per row, and pagination (app/views/address-book.html:34-45). dr1-address-book-add is the type chooser: "What is the new address for?", one addressType radio group over those same seven types and a Continue button. Each type carries a hint that defines it, and the hints are as much of the requirement as the labels are, so they are quoted here in full — Place of Origin, "The address where the animals begin their journey to Great Britain"; Consignor, "This is the sender of the consignment."; Consignee, "This is the receiver or buyer of the consignment being shipped or transported."; Importer, "This is usually the same as the consignee. You can select a different person if needed."; Place of Destination, "This is where the animals will be unloaded and accommodated for at least 48 hours. If a health certificate is required, it will show this address."; Transporter, "This is the person or company responsible for transporting the consignment."; then a divider, and Branch Address, "This is the contact address of the person responsible for the consignment from when it enters Great Britain until authorities complete their checks." The labels, the hints and the divider are all defined together at app/data/address-book-address-types.js:1-38 and rendered as govuk-radios__hint at app/views/address-book-add.html:77-80. dr1-address-book-lookup is the add form: "Add address details", a "Search for an address" type-ahead writing a hidden addressBookLookupAddressId, an "Enter address manually" toggle, "Save and continue" and "Cancel and return to address book". dr1-address-book-lookup-results is that page with the type-ahead panel open over candidate addresses. dr1-address-book-lookup-manual is that page with the manual reveal open, showing nine fields under two headings: Address (Name or organisation name, Address line 1, Address line 2 (optional), Town or city, County (optional), Postcode or Zip code, Country) and Contact details (Email address, Phone number, hinted "For international numbers include the country code"). dr1-address-book-add-from-party-picker is the same add form entered from a consignment party picker, with the type chooser skipped because the section implies the type and its answer carried in a hidden addressType. dr1-address-book-view is one saved address, headed with its own name, presented as a summary list of eight of those nine facts — County (optional) is not shown — with an "Edit" button and a red "Delete" button. dr1-address-book-edit is "Edit address and contact details": all nine fields, prefilled and already open, the search hidden, "Save changes" and "Cancel". So Design release 1's book is create, read, update and delete, and every saved address carries a type.

This is the one scope question in this comparison that a person has to settle, and it is stated here rather than decided. Two previous runs dropped these screens without photographing them; this run photographed all eight and they are enumerated above. The evidence for OUT of scope is strong, and it is not the reasoning either previous run used: the Import Notification Service front door, trade-imports-ins-frontend, already implements this address book at Design release 1's own URLs — /address-book, /address-book/add, /address-book/{id}, /address-book/{id}/edit and /address-book/{id}/delete — and its add form carries exactly the nine field labels above in Design release 1's wording, down to the phone hint; the address-book service behind it already serves create, update and delete; and this frontend's own service says writing belongs to that other service (src/server/app/services/address-book/index.js:17-19). The evidence for IN scope is that Design release 1 puts the book behind a service-navigation item on the same service as the notification journey (app/views/layouts/main.html:16) and routes into it from inside a notification (app/routes.js:3598-3600), so to a user it is one service and not two. What settles it is one thing a person can state: whether the trade-imports-ins-frontend address book is the address book Design release 1 describes. It is not yet the same book in one respect that the person deciding should know about: Design release 1 types every saved address and offers a Type filter over seven types, while the INS front door's add form asks for no type, its list has no Type column, and the address book API's locked wire contract (OperatorResponse in trade-imports-address-book) carries no type or role field — so whichever service owns these pages, the seven address types are unbuilt everywhere. If the INS book is Design release 1's book, this finding is struck and the work left in this repo is the route out of a party picker, raised separately as address-book--no-route-to-add-an-address-from-a-picker because it stands whichever way this goes, and the address types, raised separately as addresses--pickers-offer-the-whole-address-book because they bite inside the notification journey today. If it is not, this becomes one add-page piece of work covering all eight screens above, plus a write path in Frontend's address-book service. controls is deliberately empty: the finding is that eight whole pages have no counterpart, and cropping any single control on them would show less than the page does.

FALSIFIED BY: Finding a route in trade-imports-animals-frontend that renders a saved-address list, add, view, edit or delete page. Searching src/server for "address-book" returns the read-only service, its client and its callers, and no registered path beginning /address-book.

finding.prototype: Design release 1 gives the trader an address book of their own, reached from a service-navigation item on every page, and eight captured screens describe it. dr1-address-book is the list: heading "Address book", intro "Manage your addresses for use across import notifications.", a primary "Add a new address" button, a "Filter addresses" panel holding a Search box placeholdered "Search by name, address or country" and a "Type" select offering Place of Origin, Consignor, Consignee, Importer, Place of Destination, Transporter and Branch Address, a result count ("Showing 1-8 of 58"), a Name / Type / Address / Country table with a "View" link per row, and pagination (app/views/address-book.html:34-45). dr1-address-book-add is the type chooser: "What is the new address for?", one addressType radio group over those same seven types and a Continue button. Each type carries a hint that defines it, and the hints are as much of the requirement as the labels are, so they are quoted here in full — Place of Origin, "The address where the animals begin their journey to Great Britain"; Consignor, "This is the sender of the consignment."; Consignee, "This is the receiver or buyer of the consignment being shipped or transported."; Importer, "This is usually the same as the consignee. You can select a different person if needed."; Place of Destination, "This is where the animals will be unloaded and accommodated for at least 48 hours. If a health certificate is required, it will show this address."; Transporter, "This is the person or company responsible for transporting the consignment."; then a divider, and Branch Address, "This is the contact address of the person responsible for the consignment from when it enters Great Britain until authorities complete their checks." The labels, the hints and the divider are all defined together at app/data/address-book-address-types.js:1-38 and rendered as govuk-radios__hint at app/views/address-book-add.html:77-80. dr1-address-book-lookup is the add form: "Add address details", a "Search for an address" type-ahead writing a hidden addressBookLookupAddressId, an "Enter address manually" toggle, "Save and continue" and "Cancel and return to address book". dr1-address-book-lookup-results is that page with the type-ahead panel open over candidate addresses. dr1-address-book-lookup-manual is that page with the manual reveal open, showing nine fields under two headings: Address (Name or organisation name, Address line 1, Address line 2 (optional), Town or city, County (optional), Postcode or Zip code, Country) and Contact details (Email address, Phone number, hinted "For international numbers include the country code"). dr1-address-book-add-from-party-picker is the same add form entered from a consignment party picker, with the type chooser skipped because the section implies the type and its answer carried in a hidden addressType. dr1-address-book-view is one saved address, headed with its own name, presented as a summary list of eight of those nine facts — County (optional) is not shown — with an "Edit" button and a red "Delete" button. dr1-address-book-edit is "Edit address and contact details": all nine fields, prefilled and already open, the search hidden, "Save changes" and "Cancel". So Design release 1's book is create, read, update and delete, and every saved address carries a type.
finding.difference: This is the one scope question in this comparison that a person has to settle, and it is stated here rather than decided. Two previous runs dropped these screens without photographing them; this run photographed all eight and they are enumerated above. The evidence for OUT of scope is strong, and it is not the reasoning either previous run used: the Import Notification Service front door, trade-imports-ins-frontend, already implements this address book at Design release 1's own URLs — /address-book, /address-book/add, /address-book/{id}, /address-book/{id}/edit and /address-book/{id}/delete — and its add form carries exactly the nine field labels above in Design release 1's wording, down to the phone hint; the address-book service behind it already serves create, update and delete; and this frontend's own service says writing belongs to that other service (src/server/app/services/address-book/index.js:17-19). The evidence for IN scope is that Design release 1 puts the book behind a service-navigation item on the same service as the notification journey (app/views/layouts/main.html:16) and routes into it from inside a notification (app/routes.js:3598-3600), so to a user it is one service and not two. What settles it is one thing a person can state: whether the trade-imports-ins-frontend address book is the address book Design release 1 describes. It is not yet the same book in one respect that the person deciding should know about: Design release 1 types every saved address and offers a Type filter over seven types, while the INS front door's add form asks for no type, its list has no Type column, and the address book API's locked wire contract (OperatorResponse in trade-imports-address-book) carries no type or role field — so whichever service owns these pages, the seven address types are unbuilt everywhere. If the INS book is Design release 1's book, this finding is struck and the work left in this repo is the route out of a party picker, raised separately as address-book--no-route-to-add-an-address-from-a-picker because it stands whichever way this goes, and the address types, raised separately as addresses--pickers-offer-the-whole-address-book because they bite inside the notification journey today. If it is not, this becomes one add-page piece of work covering all eight screens above, plus a write path in Frontend's address-book service. controls is deliberately empty: the finding is that eight whole pages have no counterpart, and cropping any single control on them would show less than the page does.
finding.correction: Two changes. (1) The author wrote that dr1-address-book-view presents "those same nine facts". It presents eight: dr1-address-book-view.html has exactly eight govuk-summary-list__key rows — Name or organisation name, Address line 1, Address line 2 (optional), Town or city, Postcode or Zip code, Country, Email address, Phone number — and County (optional) is absent, which the screenshot confirms. The prototype slot now says eight of the nine, and says "all nine" of the edit page, where all nine labels are present (dr1-address-book-edit.html carries address-book-manual-county). (2) The difference slot's settling question is unchanged, but one true fact bearing directly on it was missing and has been added: the INS front door implements Design release 1's URLs and field labels but not its type model — its add form asks no address type, its list has no Type column, and the address-book API's wire contract carries no type or role field. Everything else the author claimed was checked and stands, including the eight-screen enumeration, the INS URL set, the INS field labels, and the read-only service comment quoted verbatim. (3) NOT A CORRECTION — AN ADDITION, MADE BY THE CORPUS EDITOR BEFORE THE FIRST INGEST, RECORDED HERE SO THE CHANGE IS NOT SILENT. The prototype slot said the seven addressType radios came "each with its own hint" without quoting them, while quoting the nine manual-entry field labels verbatim beside it. increments.title: Frontend's contact-address page explains what selecting does; Design release 1 explains who the contact is and what they are responsible for

increments.title: Frontend asks for the CPH number as one nine-character box; Design release 1 asks for it as three boxes sized to the county, parish and holding parts
increments.detail:
The County Parish Holding page renders a single text input ten characters wide, hinted "For example, 123456789 or 123/456/789." (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/cph-number/template.njk:11-23, copy at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/cph-number/copy/copy.en.js:3-6). A trader may type the number with or without slashes; the controller strips any slashes and then requires exactly nine digits (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/cph-number/controller.js:34-40,73-79). Nothing on the page tells the trader that the nine digits are two, then three, then four, and nothing stops them mistyping the split.

The boxes are two, three and four characters wide, each numeric-only and capped by `maxlength`, and each carries a label — County, Parish, Holding number — that is present for screen readers but hidden from sight, so on the page a trader meets three boxes whose widths and hint carry the format. The captured screenshot dr1-cph-number-details-open shows this: three unlabelled boxes of increasing width beneath the worked example.

Replace the single CPH input with a three-part input: county (2 digits), parish (3 digits), holding number (4 digits), numeric input mode, capped at their own lengths, under one legend and the hint "For example 12/345/6789". Keep the nine-digit rule as the combined validation. The page even carries the hint that invites the shortcut — the Importer row reads "This is usually the same as the consignee. A trader whose importer, consignee and place of destination are one company searches the book and picks the same row three times.

Design release 1 puts a second action beside "Add" on exactly the rows where a copy makes sense, and only once there is something to copy. When a consignee has been chosen, the Importer and Place of destination rows each gain a "Same as consignee" control; when a place of origin has been chosen, the Consignor row gains "Same as place of origin" (app/views/roles-and-addresses.html:83-101, availability decided at app/routes.js:2118-2133). The frontend's hub is already a POST form with a hidden crumb (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/template.njk:11-15) and the parties table already carries the ids the copy needs (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/parties.js:20-57), so nothing has to land first. increments.title: Frontend's consignment addresses list shows only the chosen party's name; Design release 1 shows the whole address the trader picked
increments.detail:
Once a party has been chosen, the Consignment addresses page shows the party's name and nothing else. In the captured answered state the five rows read "Astra Rosales", "Tech Imports Ltd", "Origin Farm", "British Livestock Ltd" and "Import Co UK", each beside a "Change" link, with no street, town, postcode or country anywhere on the page. The row value is the record's name alone (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/controller.js:32-53, which passes `parties[party.id]?.name` as the summary-list value at :49). A trader who has picked the wrong record of two with similar names cannot tell from this page; to check it they have to reopen the picker, because nothing else in the addresses section shows the address again. It reappears only on the check-your-answers page at the end of the journey, which does render every party as a name and a full address.

Design release 1 prints the selected address in full inside an inset block under each party heading — the name in bold, then every address line, then the postcode and country on the last line, then "Change" (app/views/roles-and-addresses.html:59-68). In the captured answered state Place of origin reads Green Valley Farm / Str. Principală nr. 45 / Sat Sânpetru / Comuna Sânpetru / Jud. Brașov / 507190, Romania. The CPH row uses the same inset and prints the number.

Show the selected address, not just the name, in every answered row of the Consignment addresses page: name, then the address lines, then postcode and country. The data is already in reach — the picker's own "View details" expander renders exactly these lines from `detailLines` (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/party-picker/view-model/address-lines.js:15-22) and the hub already resolves the full party record before rendering (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/controller.js:55-59). Nothing else has to land first. Note that the frontend's rows are a govuk summary list and Design release 1's are headed sections with an inset; the requirement is that the address is visible, not that the component matches. `controls` is deliberately empty: the difference runs down all six rows of the page, and the only named control on a row, "Change", occurs six times and would be refused a crop anyway.

increments.title: Frontend's address pickers show five addresses at a time and make the trader submit a search to narrow them; Design release 1 lists every address and filters it as the trader types
increments.detail:
Each of the five party pickers shows five addresses at a time under numbered pagination — the captured place-of-origin picker reads "Showing 5 of 13 addresses" over pages 1, 2, 3 and a Next link. Narrowing the list means typing into the Search box and pressing a separate secondary "Search" button, which posts the form and re-renders the page (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/party-picker/_address-picker.njk:69-110, handled at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/party-picker/party-picker.controller.js:95-104). Paging is a link, so there is no client-side script at all. A search that matches nothing replaces the whole table with one sentence, "No addresses match your search.", leaving the trader on a page with a Save and continue button and nothing to select. Page size is fixed at five (src/server/app/services/address-book/index.js:10).

Design release 1 lists every address for that party on one page and reports "Showing 9 out of 9 results" above the table. The search box is a `type="search"` input with a small magnifier button beside it, and typing filters the rows in the browser as the trader types — each row carries the text it is matched against and is hidden or shown on every keystroke, with the visible count updating in place (app/assets/javascripts/consignment-address-search.js:66-92). The captured filtered state shows "Romania" typed and the count reading "Showing 3 out of 9 results" with the page never reloaded. There is no pagination anywhere on the page and no submit involved in searching.

Replace the picker's server-side search and pagination with a full list the trader filters in the browser: render every address for that party, report "Showing N out of M results" above the table, and narrow the rows as the trader types rather than on a button press. The two halves are one change and should not be split — dropping the pagination without the live filter leaves a long list with a submit-to-search box, which is worse than either design. Two consequences to settle while doing it. First, the page size lives in the address-book service (src/server/app/services/address-book/index.js:10) and the service pages against the address-book API, so listing everything means asking that service for the whole book for an organisation rather than a page of it. Second, the picker must keep working without JavaScript; the existing Search button and paging links are the no-JS path and should stay as the fallback rather than being deleted. The empty result also stops being a dead sentence once the count is live, but the wording of "No addresses match your search." is part of the address-book route-out work raised separately.

The captured DOM of dr1-consignment-address-select carries no pagination element and its search button is `type="button"`; fe-address-picker-place-of-origin carries a `govuk-pagination` nav and a submit button named `action` with value `search`.

increments.title: Frontend squeezes the address picker's five-column results table into the narrow form column, so every row wraps onto three lines; Design release 1 gives the picker the full page width
increments.detail:
All five party pickers render inside the same two-thirds column every other journey page uses, and the results table does not fit it. In the captured place-of-origin picker the table's five columns — the radio, Name, Address, Country and the View details link — are packed into the left two-thirds of the page, and every row wraps: "Astra Rosales" breaks over two lines, "43 East Hague Extension, Bern, 30055" over three, "United Kingdom" over two, and "View details" over two, on all five rows. Roughly a third of the page beside the table is empty. The width is not a decision the picker takes: the shared layout reads it from `contentColumnClass` (src/server/app/shared/layout.njk:56-57), and `kit.base` hardcodes that to the form surface, `govuk-grid-column-two-thirds` (src/server/app/shared/kit.js:20-23 and :122). The picker's controller builds its view context from `kit.base` and passes nothing that would change it (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/party-picker/party-picker.controller.js:43-47).

Design release 1 gives the picker the whole width of the page — its view opens on `govuk-grid-column-full` (app/views/consignment-address-select.html:27) — and it is a decision taken for this page rather than a house style, because the two other addresses pages the same release serves stay in the two-thirds column: roles-and-addresses and contact-address-for-consignment both render there. The result is that every row of the captured picker reads on one line: name, then the address lines stacked one per line because the design breaks them deliberately rather than because they wrap, then the country, then "View details" against the right-hand edge.

Render the five party pickers on the full-width surface. Frontend already has one and already uses it elsewhere: `SURFACES.display` is `govuk-grid-column-full` (src/server/app/shared/kit.js:20-23), and the dashboard picks it up by spreading `contentColumnClass: surfaceClass('display')` after `kit.base` (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/dashboard/controller.js:71). The picker needs the same one line at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/party-picker/party-picker.controller.js:43. Nothing has to land first. Sequence it after addresses--picker-pages-results-and-searches-on-the-server, which changes how many rows the table holds and therefore how much of the width the change buys. Two notes for whoever picks this up. Design release 1 also declares full width on its CPH page (app/views/cph-number.html:27), but that page holds one short field and nothing on it overflows the form column, so the work here is the pickers and not every page the design widens. And although the frontend's column width is set in shared code, this is not a service-wide finding: the design does not widen every page — it widens this one — so what has to change is which surface the picker asks for, not the default. `controls` is deliberately empty: what differs is the width of the page itself, so the whole-page shot is the only picture that shows it and a crop of any one control would hide the point.

FALSIFIED BY: Finding Frontend's address picker rendered on anything other than `govuk-grid-column-two-thirds`, or Design release 1's picker rendered on anything other than `govuk-grid-column-full`.

increments.title: Frontend offers the trader's entire address book on all six address pickers; Design release 1 offers only the addresses saved for that role, and only branch addresses for the contact
increments.detail:
All five party pickers and the contact-address page draw from one undifferentiated list. Every captured picker reports "Showing 5 of 13 addresses" and every one of them offers the same thirteen records in the same order, whether the trader is choosing a place of origin abroad or a consignee in Great Britain — the place-of-origin picker and the consignee picker both lead with Astra Rosales in Switzerland, Tech Imports Ltd in London and Origin Farm in Ireland. Those two pickers are byte-identical in the captured DOM — same caption, same five rows in the same order, the remaining eight behind the same pagination — so the page that asks for the farm the animals left offers Great Britain importers, and the page that asks who is receiving them offers foreign farms. The contact-address page lists the same book again, all thirteen as radios (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/contact/controller.js:69-75, which calls `addressBook.all`). This is deliberate: the address-book service states that addresses have no type, because the same record may be a consignor on one notification and a consignee on the next, and so no function it exposes takes a role (src/server/app/services/address-book/index.js:12-15). The picker controller calls the book with a query and a page number and nothing else (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/party-picker/party-picker.controller.js:36), so no amount of real data changes what these pages offer: there is no field to filter on. The consequence for the trader is that every picker asks them to find the right kind of address in a list that is mostly the wrong kind, with nothing on the page marking which is which.

Design release 1 types every saved address and filters each picker to its type. Place of origin offers nine foreign farms, consignor nine, consignee six Great Britain importers, importer six, place of destination three — different lists, from the same book, with the section's own type deciding what appears (app/routes.js:3457-3466 and app/routes.js:3520-3543). The types are the trader's own: saving an address begins by asking "What is the new address for?" over Place of Origin, Consignor, Consignee, Importer, Place of Destination, Transporter and, after a divider, Branch Address (app/data/address-book-address-types.js:1-38). The contact address is the Branch Address type, held as its own list of the organisation's branches (app/data/contact-addresses.js:1-21), which is why Design release 1's contact page says "add a new branch address" rather than "add an address".

Give a saved address one or more roles and filter each picker by the role it is asking for, including the contact page, which asks only for a branch address. The frontend cannot do this alone: its address-book service reads a book that carries no type at all and exposes no role-aware call (src/server/app/services/address-book/index.js:12-19), so the address-book API — the Standard Address Block records in trade-imports-address-book — has to carry the type first, and whichever service writes those records has to collect it. Decide it together with the address-book scope question raised as address-book--saved-address-book-pages-absent, because the type is collected on the add form that question is about. This is a live defect in the notification journey whichever way that scope question is settled: it is about what the pickers Frontend already has show today, not about pages Frontend does not have, so it survives a ruling that the eight address-book screens belong to another service. Until the type exists, no useful half of this can ship: filtering on a guess, such as matching the country against the direction of travel, would hide addresses the trader legitimately wants. `controls` is deliberately empty: what differs is which rows are in the table, so the whole table on each of two pickers is the shot, and the only named control on those rows, `party`, occurs once per row and would be refused a crop.

increments.title: For commodity code 01061900 Design release 1 lists each chosen species as its own removable row in Selected commodities; Frontend gives the commodity one row and one Remove that drops every species under it.
increments.detail:
The Selected commodities table carries one row per commodity, whatever was chosen inside it. The captured page shows "01061900 / Dog / Remove" as a single row, and the table is built by collapsing the commodity lines to their distinct commodity names (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/consignment-details/view-model/groups.js:24-33, rendered at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/consignment-details/_selected-commodities-table.njk:4-19). Pressing Remove drops every line of that commodity at once (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/consignment-details/remove/post-remove.js:26-40). A user who has chosen two species under one 01061900 commodity has no way to drop one of them from this page — the only route back is to reopen the commodity page and untick it there.

Every commodity gets one row except those on commodity code 01061900, which get one row per chosen species, each named by that species' own common name and each carrying its own Remove (app/routes.js:626-645, against app/routes.js:672-682 for every other commodity). Removing one takes that species out and leaves the rest of the commodity in place. Design release 1's captured page shows cattle, which is not 01061900, so the picture shows the ordinary commodity-level row and this rule has to be read from where it is stated.

On the consignment-details page, list each chosen species of a 01061900 commodity as its own row in Selected commodities, named by the species, with a Remove that takes out that species only and leaves the rest of the commodity. Everything else keeps the commodity-level row it has now. The frontend's stub already carries two commodities on that code — Cat and Dog (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/services/commodities/stub.js:3-10) — and the difference already shows today even with one species each, because a per-species row is named by the species rather than by the commodity: on Design release 1 the dog row reads "Domestic dog", on Frontend it reads "Dog". A second species under either would then add a second row where Frontend still shows one. Removal already works line by line underneath: the store holds one line per species and only the page collapses them, so this is a change to the table and to what Remove submits rather than to the store. Nothing has to land first.

FALSIFIED BY: Design release 1 rendering a single commodity-level row for a 01061900 commodity with two species chosen — for instance ferret and dog together. The selected-rows builder branches on the code before it branches on anything else, so a single row there would prove this wrong.

increments.title: On the commodity-details page Frontend sets the commodity heading, the species name and the quantity labels smaller and lighter than Design release 1, so the page loses the reading order the design gives it.
increments.detail:
Below the page heading the type steps down twice and then flattens. The commodity heading "Cow (0102)" is a medium heading, the species name "Bos taurus" below it is a small heading, and the two field labels — "Number of animals" and "Number of packages (optional)" — carry no size or weight at all, so they render in ordinary body text at the same size and weight as the hints under them (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/consignment-details/_species-quantities.njk:7, :9, :14 and :26). With four commodities on the captured page, the labels and the hints form an unbroken run of same-weight text and only the two headings break it up.

The same block is set three sizes larger throughout. The commodity heading "Cattle (0102)" is 36px bold — the size of the page heading itself — the species name "Bos taurus" below it is 24px bold, and every field label on the page is 19px bold against a 19px light hint, so each question stands away from its own guidance (app/assets/sass/application.scss:1070-1112, the app-consignment-details-page block, whose .govuk-label rule at :1107-1112 sets weight 700). The captured page shows all three levels.

Raise the three levels on the commodity-details page to match: the per-commodity heading, the species name beneath it, and the labels on the quantity inputs. One template carries all of them. Nothing has to land first, and it is independent of the other commodity-details changes — the page rename, the package label and the animal-count rule — though it is cheapest done in the same pass. Note that Design release 1 sets the per-commodity heading at the same size as the page heading, which is a deliberate step and not a slip: the commodity blocks are the substance of the page and the heading above them is only its name.

increments.title: Frontend refuses to let a user lower the number of animals below the identification records already entered for that species; Design release 1 accepts the lower number and shows only that many records.
increments.detail:
A user who has entered identification details for two Bos taurus and then comes back and changes the count to 1 is held on the page. The error summary and the field both read "You have 2 identifier records for Bos taurus but entered 1 animal. Remove identifier records or keep the higher count.", and the summary link sends the user to the identification card for that line rather than to the box they just typed in. Nothing is saved until they either put the number back up or go and delete records by hand (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/consignment-details/validation/count-drop.js:13-33).

The same change is accepted. The count is checked only for presence and for being a whole number of at least one (app/routes.js:817-848); there is no comparison against what has already been entered, and no message of that kind exists anywhere in Design release 1. The identification page then draws exactly as many animal slots as the new count asks for, so the surplus record simply stops being shown and stops counting towards completeness.

Stop refusing the submission. Follow Design release 1: accept the lower count and let the identification page show that many records. What the frontend does with the surplus record has to be decided as part of the work — Design release 1 leaves it in the session and stops rendering it, so it neither warns nor deletes — and whichever way that goes, the user is no longer stopped at the consignment-details page. Removing the rule takes the message out of the commodities copy file with it (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/copy/copy.en.js:38-39) and the Welsh file beside it. Nothing has to land first.

FALSIFIED BY: Design release 1 refusing a reduced count, or warning about surplus identification records. Its consignment-details handler runs four validators — animals, packages, net weight and package type — and none of them reads the saved identifiers; a fifth check, or any message naming identifier records, would prove this wrong.

increments.title: Frontend's "Help with commodity codes" gives one sentence and no way to look a code up; Design release 1 explains what a commodity code is and links out to the Trade Tariff tool.
increments.detail:
Opening the "Help with commodity codes" details reveals a single sentence — "Commodity codes are used to classify goods for import and export." — and nothing else. It is passed to the govukDetails macro as plain text, so it cannot carry a link (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/search/search.njk:31-34, with the string at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/copy/copy.en.js:9). The details of the same name, in the same position on the page, holds three paragraphs: "Commodity codes are internationally recognised reference numbers.", "A commodity code describes a specific product when importing or exporting goods.", and "You can look up commodity codes using the Trade Tariff tool (opens in a new tab).", where "Trade Tariff tool" is a link to https://www.gov.uk/trade-tariff opening in a new tab (app/views/what-are-you-importing.html:119-132).

Replace the one-sentence help text with Design release 1's three paragraphs, including the Trade Tariff link and its "(opens in a new tab)" suffix. That means passing HTML to the details rather than text, so the copy entry changes shape as well as wording; the Welsh copy file beside it carries the same single string and needs the same treatment. increments.title: Removing the last commodity leaves the Frontend user on an empty details page with a link to start again; Design release 1 takes them straight back to "What are you importing?".

The empty-state copy and the "Add a commodity" label then have no state left to render and can go, along with the branch that chooses between the two link labels. Nothing has to land first. Neither side photographed the empty state, so the observation that would confirm the landing page on each is a removal of the only commodity.

increments.title: Frontend asks what is being imported by printing the whole commodity reference list as tick boxes; Design release 1 asks the user to search for a commodity and shows nothing until they do.
increments.detail:
The page has no search box. Under the heading "What are you importing?" it prints every commodity the reference service knows about, one tick-box group per commodity, legend "Cow (0102)", "Horse (0101)", "Cat (01061900)", "Dog (01061900)", "Fish (0301)", with a tick box per species inside each. The template loops the whole list and renders a govukCheckboxes group for each entry with no filtering step of any kind (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/search/search.njk:19-30), and the view model builds one group per commodity with no query argument (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/search/view-model/commodity-groups.js:3-15). The controller takes no query parameter and has no search action: it renders the list on GET and validates the ticked boxes on POST (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/search/search.controller.js:36-52). The captured page fits on one screen only because the stub holds five commodities and eight species between them.

The page shows one control, a search box labelled "Search for a commodity" with the hint "You can search by common name (for example, cattle), commodity code (0102), or Latin name (Bos taurus)." Nothing is listed until the user has typed at least three characters: results then appear in a panel directly under the box, grouped under a commodity header such as "Cattle (0102)" with a tick box per matching species, and the matched characters are shown in bold. Chosen species collect into a panel below the results, headed with a running count — "2 selected" — that lists each one and offers "Clear all". The search matches on the species Latin name, the species common name, the commodity name and the commodity code (app/views/what-are-you-importing.html:47-117).

Replace the printed tick-box list on the commodity page with a search: a labelled search box over the reference list, a results panel that appears once at least three characters are entered and groups matching species under their commodity heading with a tick box each, and a running list of what has been chosen so far, headed with the count, with a way to clear it. The list the frontend prints today is bounded only by what the reference service returns — the requirements side's own fixture already carries twenty-one commodities and over a hundred species under "Other live mammals" alone — so the printed list stops being usable as soon as the stub is replaced. Nothing has to land first: the reference data the search would filter is the same list the page already fetches. Keep the existing "Select a commodity" error, which both sides already use for an empty submission.

FALSIFIED BY: A search input, a filter field or a type-ahead anywhere on fe-commodity-search. The captured DOM for that page contains no input other than the CSRF hidden field and the eight species tick boxes, and the controller reads no query parameter, so finding one would prove this wrong.

increments.title: Frontend lets a user leave every "Number of animals" box empty and move on to the next page, and only refuses the notification later at the review gate; Design release 1 holds them on the page until each one is filled in.
increments.detail:

Each line gets one rule, an integer-in-range check with a minimum of one (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/consignment-details/fields.js:18-33), and that rule's schema explicitly allows the empty string, which short-circuits before the digits test runs (src/server/app/lib/validate/validators.js:123-143). increments.title: On the commodity page Frontend labels each species tick box with its Latin name alone; Design release 1 labels it with the common name and the Latin name in brackets, for example "Domestic cattle (Bos taurus)".
increments.detail:
Every tick box on the commodity page is labelled with a Latin name and nothing else — "Bison bison", "Bos spp.", "Bos taurus", "Bubalus bubalis", "Equus caballus", "Felis catus", "Canis lupus familiaris", "Salmo salar". A common name appears only in the fieldset legend for the commodity the species sits under ("Cow (0102)"), never on the box itself. The species record the view model reads carries only a value and a text, with no slot for a common name at all (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/search/view-model/commodity-groups.js:6-13). A user who knows the animal as a cow, a dog or a salmon never sees that word next to the box they have to tick.

Every species row in the results panel reads as its common name with the Latin name in brackets, and the rule holds for every species rather than for the ones the fixture happens to name: where a species carries its own common name the row is "<common name> (<Latin name>)", and where it does not the commodity's name is used instead, so "Cyprinidae" renders as "Ornamental fish (Cyprinidae)" (app/assets/javascripts/commodity-search.js:11-17). The captured results panel shows "Domestic cattle (Bos taurus)". The same pairing is what the search matches against, so typing "cattle" finds Bos taurus (app/assets/javascripts/commodity-search.js:51-55).

Label the species tick boxes on the commodity page "<common name> (<Latin name>)", falling back to the commodity's own name where the species has no common name of its own. This needs the reference data to carry a common name per species: the commodities service exposes only a value and a text per species and has no real client behind the stub (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/services/commodities/index.js:37-42, src/server/app/sets/live-animals/services/commodities/stub.js:15-26), so whether this is copy work or a reference-data change turns on what the live commodity service returns. Banded as frontend work because the rendering is the part that is wrong today; if the live service turns out not to carry a common name per species, the band moves to needs-backend. Scope it to the tick-box labels only: the species heading on the commodity-details page is the Latin name on both sides, and changing it would move Frontend away from Design release 1 rather than towards it.

FALSIFIED BY: A frontend species tick-box label that already reads as a common name — for instance the live commodity service returning "Domestic cattle" rather than "Bos taurus" in the species text — which would make this a fixture difference rather than a labelling one.

increments.title: A trader who fills in the document form and presses Continue loses it on the frontend without being told; Design release 1 saves that document, or stops them and says what is missing
increments.detail:
The page offers two ways to submit the document form and only one of them keeps anything. "Save and add another" posts action=add and saves the document. "Continue" posts action=continue from inside the same form, so the reference, the date of issue and the chosen file all travel to the server in that request — and the server never looks at them. The post handler branches on the action and reads the payload only for add and remove; every other action loads the page state fresh, checks whether any already-saved document is still being scanned, and redirects to the next page (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/controller.js:255-279). Nothing is saved, no error is shown, and the next screen gives no sign that anything was dropped. A trader who fills the three fields, chooses their health certificate and presses the primary green button — the one the whole rest of the journey has taught them to press — arrives at the next page having attached nothing. "Save and return to hub" behaves the same way.

"Save and continue" completes the document. Design release 1 treats a part-filled form as an intention to attach: if the trader has chosen a document type, it validates the whole form, and either adds the document to the notification and moves on, or stays on the page and shows the same four messages the add path would have shown, so the trader is told what is missing rather than losing the file (app/routes.js:10173-10193). Uploading remains optional — an untouched form continues without complaint. "Save and return to overview" is the one action that deliberately discards a part-filled form.

Make Continue finish the document rather than throw it away. On a Continue post, look at the add-a-document fields: if the trader has entered anything at all, run the same validation the Add path runs and either save the document and move on, or re-render the page with the field errors. Second, whether "Save and return to hub" should behave the same way — Design release 1 says no, and matching it exactly means only Continue changes.

increments.title: Frontend never tells a trader how many documents a notification may hold until they hit the limit; Design release 1 states it in the file requirements above the upload control

A trader learns the limit only by reaching it, at which point the error summary tells them (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/copy/copy.en.js:73), after they have already chosen a file and tried to upload it. increments.title: Design release 1 asks the user to pick a document type for every document they upload; the frontend never asks and guesses the type from the file's name
increments.detail:
The Upload documents page asks for three things and nothing else: Document reference, Date of issue and a file. The captured DOM of fe-documents carries exactly three named inputs on the add-a-document form — accompanyingDocumentReference, accompanyingDocumentDateOfIssue and file — and no select of any kind. A document type is nonetheless recorded and shown: the saved-documents table has a Document type column and on fe-documents-populated that column reads "Veterinary health certificate" for a document whose type the user was never asked for. The value is guessed from the uploaded file's name. The filename has its extension stripped, its separators flattened to spaces, and the result is matched word-for-word against the document-type list, longest candidate winning, falling back to 'OTHER' when nothing matches (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/derive-document-type.js:19-23); the controller stamps the guess onto the record at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/controller.js:109-111. So a trader who uploads scan001.pdf gets "Other" and one whose file happens to be called veterinary-health-certificate.pdf gets a type they never chose. Nothing shows the guess before it is saved and nothing lets a user correct it afterwards — the two actions offered on a saved row are View file and Remove, and neither changes the type; the only way out of a wrong guess is to remove the document and upload it again under a different filename. The field is mandatory in the frontend's own obligation model (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/documents.js:30-35), so the service depends on a value it never collects.

Document type is the second question on the page, sitting between Document reference and Date of issue. It is a select labelled "Document type" that opens on "Select one" and offers Intra Trade Animal Health Certificate (ITAHC), Veterinary health certificate, Air waybill, Import permit, Letter of authority (Directive 2008/61/EC), Commercial invoice, Sea waybill, Rail waybill, Bill of lading, Catch certificate, Laboratory sampling results for aflatoxin (Reg 2019/1793), Journey log and Other (app/views/upload-documents.html:115-129). It is required: on dr1-upload-documents-errors, leaving it unset produces "Select a document type" in the error summary linked to #document-type and again as an error message above the select.

Add a Document type select to the upload form, between Document reference and Date of issue, and make it required with the message "Select a document type". The list already exists in the frontend: src/server/app/services/document-types/index.js:3 exposes the enum and the user-facing labels for every member are already written at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/copy/copy.en.js:26-41. Save the chosen value as accompanyingDocumentType, which is already a mandatory field in the model and already persisted, and delete the filename derivation at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/derive-document-type.js along with its only caller at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/controller.js:111. increments.title: Design release 1 lets a trader drop a document onto the page and shows which file is chosen; the frontend offers only the browser's own file button
increments.detail:

What the trader sees on fe-documents is whatever the browser draws for a file input — on the capture, a small grey "Choose File" button with "No file chosen" beside it, in the browser's own type rather than the service's. There is no drop target, so a file cannot be dragged onto the page, and the chosen filename is shown only in the browser's own text beside the button.

The control is a dashed-outline drop zone occupying the width of the card. Inside it a status line, in a highlighted band and marked aria-live="polite", reads "No file chosen" until a file is picked and then reads the file's name; below that a styled "Choose file" button sits beside the words "or drop file" (app/views/upload-documents.html:172-179). A trader can drag a document from their desktop onto the zone, and either way the page itself tells them which file they are about to upload.

Turn on the JavaScript-enhanced file upload for this control. The frontend is on govuk-frontend 6.3, whose file upload component provides exactly this behaviour — a drop zone, a "Choose file" button, the words "or drop file" and a live region naming the chosen file — when the component is asked for it and its JavaScript is initialised. increments.title: The frontend rejects any document over 10 MB; Design release 1 allows files up to 50MB
increments.detail:
The upload control's hint reads "Your file must be:" over two bullets, the first of which is "smaller than 10 MB". The limit is enforced twice — in the browser, from a data-max-file-size attribute of 10000000 on the form element, and on the server, where a file over the limit is refused with "The selected file must be smaller than 10 MB" (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/form/errors.js:34-36). Ten decimal megabytes is a deliberate choice made against the platform rather than against the design: the code says so, at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/upload-config.js:40-46, where the comment records that the value stays clear of the 10 MiB nginx ingress cap on the hosting platform. So a trader with a 20 MB scanned health certificate cannot attach it and is given no alternative on the page.

The same hint list opens with "files that are smaller than 50MB" (app/views/upload-documents.html:166). Design release 1 states 50MB as the ceiling a trader may upload to.

Raise the accepted file size from 10 MB to 50MB and change the hint bullet and the oversize error message to match. The value and its label live in one place, src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/upload-config.js:40-46, and the browser-side check reads the same number from the form's data-max-file-size attribute, so the frontend edit is small. It is banded needs-backend because the frontend cannot make the change alone: the code records that 10 MB was chosen to stay under the platform's 10 MiB ingress limit, so the request-body cap on the hosting platform's ingress and on whatever receives the upload has to be raised to at least 50MB first, otherwise a large file will be rejected by the infrastructure before the service sees it and the trader will get a platform error page instead of a validation message. Confirm the ceiling with the document-upload service before changing the number.

increments.title: Frontend caps a notification at 10 accompanying documents; Design release 1 allows 15
increments.detail:
A notification may hold at most ten documents. The cap is an obligation on the documents group (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/documents.js:24-27) and the page reads it from there (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/contracts/max-documents.js:3). A trader who chooses an eleventh file is refused on submit, with an error summary reading "You can add a maximum of 10 documents" (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/copy/copy.en.js:73).

Design release 1 allows fifteen. That number backs the validation, which refuses a sixteenth with "You can upload a maximum of 15 files" (app/routes.js:9106-9109), and it is also the number stated in the hint above the upload control (app/views/upload-documents.html:168).

Raise the cap from 10 to 15 at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/documents.js:25. That one value is read by the page, the Add affordance and the error message, so nothing else has to move: the error copy at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/copy/copy.en.js:73 already interpolates the number. Update the obligation file's own header comment with it, which describes the group as 0..10 at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/documents.js:2-16. This lands entirely in Frontend and the band is frontend-work: the cap is a frontend obligation constant and has no counterpart on the wire — its only non-test uses are the error message and the submit guard, and no other service is told the number. Stating the limit on the page before a trader chooses a file is a separate change, raised as documents--document-limit-not-stated-before-a-file-is-chosen. The two are independently schedulable in either order: the frontend could state its current limit of ten today without touching the cap, and the cap could be raised without the page ever mentioning it.

increments.title: Design release 1 tells a trader which documents to attach before the upload form; the frontend goes straight to the form with no guidance at all
increments.detail:
Between the "Upload documents" heading and the first field there is nothing. The captured DOM of fe-documents goes from the h1 straight into the form and the Document reference label, and the whole page contains no paragraph of body copy, no bulleted list of document kinds, no details expander and no link out to GOV.UK guidance. A trader arriving on the page is told what to type but never what to attach or why: the words ITAHC, licence, invoice and certificate appear nowhere on the frontend page outside the saved-documents table.

The page opens with three pieces of guidance before the form. First a paragraph: "You must attach an ITAHC if this consignment requires one. If you do not have it now, you can add it later. All documents should be uploaded before the consignment arrives at the UK port. Documents must be in English and you must upload all pages." Then "Other documents you may need to attach include:" over a bulleted list of "import licences or authorisations" and "commercial documents or invoices". Then a closed details expander, "Check which additional documents you must upload", holding a two-column table headed Consignment / Documents needed with three rows — animals that do not need a health certificate need an exporter's declaration that they are fit to travel; livestock transiting bluetongue restricted territories need Bluetongue declaration GBHC172; rodents imported for research purposes need an RM39 licence and supplementary health certificate — followed by "Check the documents you need on GOV.UK (opens in a new tab)", linked to the GOV.UK import-of-products guidance. All of it is stated at app/views/upload-documents.html:37-79.

Add the guidance block to the frontend's documents template above the form: the intro paragraph, the "Other documents you may need to attach include" list, and a govukDetails expander holding the three-row table and the GOV.UK link. The copy belongs in src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/copy/copy.en.js and the markup in src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/template.njk:16-17, before the form element opens. This is content only — no new field, no validation, no service call — so it can be built today. The GOV.UK href in Design release 1 carries prototype analytics parameters; use the clean guidance URL. Raised as one finding rather than three because it is one block of page content that only makes sense together. It names no control deliberately: the difference is a block of prose above the form, not a field, and the whole-page shot is the right picture for it.

increments.title: Design release 1 tells a trader that ZIP files are not allowed and why; the frontend refuses them silently and gives a message that never mentions ZIP
increments.detail:

increments.title: The hub hides the animal and package totals until a commodity has been added, where Design release 1 shows them from the start reading zero
increments.detail:
On a notification with no commodities the hub goes straight from the "Overview" heading to the first task section. There is no "Your commodities" heading and no summary of what the notification contains — the words appear in no captured frontend screen in this corpus. The frontend does build the same two summary panels, headed "Your commodities" with the labels "Animals" and "Packages/boxes" and the same captions (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/hub/copy/copy.en.js:3-9, rendered at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/hub/template.njk:8-26), but the whole block is behind a truthiness test and the view model returns null while the commodity collection is empty (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/hub/controller.js:142-151), so a user only ever meets it once they have added a commodity line.

Design release 1 shows "Your commodities" directly under the page heading on every visit to the hub, with two grey panels reading "0 Animals — Total number of animals in this consignment" and "0 Packages/boxes — Total number of packages in this consignment" before anything has been entered, and the same panels reading the real totals once commodities exist (app/views/notification-hub.html:26-50). The summary is the first thing on the page and it is never absent.

Render the commodity summary on every visit to the hub, showing zero for both totals when the notification holds no commodity lines, instead of suppressing the block. The change is the null return at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/hub/controller.js:142-151 and the guard around the block at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/hub/template.njk:8. One layout consequence travels with it and is worth stating rather than raising twice: both sides lay the two panels out as a pair of half-width columns, but Design release 1 gives the hub the full grid width (app/views/notification-hub.html:21) while the frontend confines it to a two-thirds column, so the panels arrive narrower than the design draws them.

FALSIFIED BY: Finding the string "Your commodities" in the captured DOM of any frontend screen in this corpus. It appears in the two prototype hub captures and in no frontend capture.

increments.title: The hub lists an animal identification task on a notification with no commodities, where Design release 1 adds that task only once a commodity needs identifiers
increments.detail:
"Animal identification details" is on the hub from the moment the notification is created, before any commodity has been chosen and therefore before it is known whether any animal needs an identifier at all. It shows on both captured hub states, locked with the status "Cannot start yet". The frontend does know how to leave a row out — its exit-details and transit-countries rows are marked conditional and are absent from both captures (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/flow/task-rows.js:35-47, with the hiding at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/hub/controller.js:93-118) — but the identification row is not marked that way (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/flow/task-rows.js:41-45), so it always appears.

Design release 1's hub has no identification task on a notification with nothing chosen: its "2. Description of the goods" section holds two rows, "Commodity details" and "Additional details". "Identification details" is inserted between them only when the commodities chosen require animal identifiers (app/routes.js:5778-5782), which is what dr1-notification-hub-partly-complete shows. So the task appears when it becomes relevant and is invisible until then.

Make the identification row conditional on the notification actually needing animal identifiers, so it is absent from the hub rather than present and locked while no commodity has been chosen. The hub already knows how to drop a row — src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/hub/controller.js:93 hides a row that is marked conditional once its status is not-applicable — but marking the identification entry conditional at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/flow/task-rows.js:41-45 is not on its own enough, and the work has to allow for that. The row's status is rolled up over the commodityLines collection (:44), and commodityLines is a structural group that is in scope from the moment the notification exists (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/commodities/lines.js:18-32), so the roll-up never reaches not-applicable and the row would still be drawn. Either the row needs its own applicability test — do any chosen commodities require identifiers, which is the question Design release 1 asks at app/routes.js:5778 — or the identification obligations need a scope condition that makes the roll-up not-applicable with no commodity lines. This is a different change from unlocking the rows (hub--task-rows-locked-until-earlier-work-is-done): unlocking makes a shown row usable, this decides whether the row is shown at all.
