So the task appears when it becomes relevant and is invisible until then.
finding.difference: Make the identification row conditional on the notification actually needing animal identifiers, so it is absent from the hub rather than present and locked while no commodity has been chosen. The hub already knows how to drop a row — src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/hub/controller.js:93 hides a row that is marked conditional once its status is not-applicable — but marking the identification entry conditional at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/flow/task-rows.js:41-45 is not on its own enough, and the work has to allow for that. The row's status is rolled up over the commodityLines collection (:44), and commodityLines is a structural group that is in scope from the moment the notification exists (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/commodities/lines.js:18-32), so the roll-up never reaches not-applicable and the row would still be drawn. Either the row needs its own applicability test — do any chosen commodities require identifiers, which is the question Design release 1 asks at app/routes.js:5778 — or the identification obligations need a scope condition that makes the roll-up not-applicable with no commodity lines. finding.correction: The two observation slots are correct as written and were left alone. The difference slot claimed "The machinery already exists: add the conditional flag ... and the hub will drop the row when its status is not applicable." That is wrong, and it would have sent a developer to a one-line change that does nothing. The hiding test is isHiddenRow at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/hub/controller.js:93, which needs both row.conditional and a status of NA. A row's status is statusOf over its parts, and statusOf returns NA only when no part is in scope, comparing on the part's collection name (src/server/app/bridge/status/index.js:87-91 with src/server/app/bridge/status/classification/index.js:12). The identification row's part is the commodityLines collection filtered to animalIdentifiers (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/flow/task-rows.js:41-45), so the key it tests is commodityLines — and commodityLines carries no applyTo and is declared always in scope (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/commodities/lines.js:18-32), which src/server/app/bridge/scope.js:96-120 projects into the scope set unconditionally. So the status is never NA and the flag alone would leave the row on the page. This is also why the exit-details and transit-countries comparison does not carry over: those rows roll up over scalar obligations that genuinely leave scope when the import reason is unanswered. The difference slot now states the real shape of the work.

Read all the cited frontend lines. Rubric 1 (a claim about the fix that the code does not support) fired on the difference slot — see correction. The finding's substance is unaffected and stands at high confidence.

increments.title: Halfway through a new notification the frontend sends the user back to the hub and makes them start each remaining section from it, where Design release 1 carries straight on and runs the whole notification through in one sequence
increments.detail:
A new notification is walked through seven questions and then dropped on the hub. The sequence is origin, what are you importing, consignment details, main reason for importing, purpose in the internal market, animal identification and additional animal details (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/flow/run.js:22-39); pressing "Save and continue" on the last of them does not go to the arrival details, it goes to the hub, because the sequence has run out and the fall-through returns the hub path (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/flow/run.js:41-53). From there the pattern repeats for the rest of the notification: every later section is entered from a task row and ends by returning to the hub, because the within-section next target also falls through to the hub when a section has no further page (src/server/app/flow/navigation.js:27-37). The four sections still to answer at that point — documents, addresses, transport and the consignment contact (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/flow/flow.js:59-80) — are therefore four separate departures from the task list and four returns to it.

Design release 1 has one sequence and runs it end to end. Its steps are origin, what are you importing, reason for import, consignment details, animal identification where it applies, additional details, arrival details, transit countries where they apply, transporter, upload documents, roles and addresses, contact address, review and declaration (app/routes.js:1256-1285), and saving a page moves to the next step in that list (app/routes.js:1287-1305). Pressing "Save and continue" on the additional animal details takes the user to the arrival details (app/routes.js:9533). The hub is somewhere a user chooses to go — by pressing the secondary "Save and return to overview", or by opening the notification from the dashboard — not somewhere the journey puts them, so a user who follows the primary button reaches the declaration without seeing it.

Carry the sequence on past the additional animal details instead of ending it there, so "Save and continue" moves to the next question in the notification and the user reaches the review page in one pass. That means the opening run at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/flow/run.js:22-39 stops being an opening run and becomes the whole journey, in Design release 1's order — arrival details, transit countries where they apply, transporter, upload documents, roles and addresses, contact address, then review — and the fall-through to the hub at :41-53 and at src/server/app/flow/navigation.js:36 applies only at the end of the journey rather than at the end of every section. The hub stays reachable throughout: both sides already put a secondary "Save and return to overview" button on each page, so nothing has to be added to get back to it. This is not the same change as unlocking the hub's rows (hub--task-rows-locked-until-earlier-work-is-done): that one decides what a user can start from the task list, this one decides whether they are sent to the task list at all.

FALSIFIED BY: Saving the frontend's additional-animal-details page and landing on a journey page rather than on the hub. This run's own frontend capture asserts the opposite — after the additional-details page is saved it asserts the URL is the bare journey path, which is the hub — so finding a redirect to /arrival-details or any other page there would prove this wrong.

Contact address" holding the contact row; and delete the "6. Check and submit" section, whose row is replaced by a button (see hub--no-review-and-submit-button). increments.title: The frontend locks all but one hub task behind the answers before it, while Design release 1 lets a user start any task on the notification in any order
increments.detail:
On a brand new notification the hub lists eleven tasks and exactly one of them can be opened. "Where is this consignment coming from?" is a link tagged "Not yet started"; the other ten rows are plain text with the grey status "Cannot start yet" and carry no link at all, so the hub offers no way into them. Answering the origin questions unlocks precisely one more row — on fe-hub-part-answered "What are you importing?" has become a link and every row below it still reads "Cannot start yet", including "Arrival details", "Upload documents" and "Contact address", none of which depends on the origin answers. The hub decides this per row: src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/hub/controller.js:120-122 renders an open row or a blocked one according to whether the first page in the row passes its gate, and the gate is that page's prerequisites at src/server/app/flow/gates.js:23-32.

Every task on the hub is a link from the moment the notification is created, and every one carries the same status, "To do". A user can open "Upload documents", "Roles and addresses" or "Contact address for this consignment" before saying anything about the consignment, and can come back to "Main reason for import" afterwards. Design release 1 renders each row as an unconditional link (app/views/notification-hub.html:60-73) and offers no locked state and no "cannot start" wording anywhere on the page.

Drop the row gating on the hub so every task row renders as a link with a real status from the moment the notification exists, and retire the "Cannot start yet" status the hub uses for a blocked row. The gate to remove is the one the hub itself consults: rowGatePasses tests the row's first page against the per-page prerequisites at src/server/app/flow/gates.js:23-32 (src/server/app/flow/navigation.js:25), and the hub renders an open or a blocked row on that answer. The change does not stop at the hub, but the work is smaller than it looks in one respect and larger in another. Smaller, because nothing has to be unblocked at the route: no request handler consults those prerequisites, the only pre-handler guard being the deep-link entry guard at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/flow/entry-guard.js:45-57, so the pages already admit a direct visit. Larger, because that is exactly why they have never had to cope: each page behind an unlocked row has to render and save sensibly when the pages that currently precede it have not been answered. Where a page genuinely cannot be answered until something else is known — the animal identifiers need a commodity — Design release 1's answer is to leave the row out of the list until it applies, not to show it locked; that is its own finding, hub--identification-row-shown-before-it-applies.

FALSIFIED BY: Finding a second link on the frontend's hub for an unanswered notification. The captured DOM of fe-hub carries exactly one element with class govuk-task-list__link and ten rows carrying govuk-task-list__status--cannot-start-yet.

increments.title: A trader who has miscounted the animals has no way out of Frontend's identification page; Design release 1 offers a Change number of animals link on every species panel
increments.detail:
Each card is headed with the commodity and species and then a counter — "Enter details for Bos taurus 1 of 2" — and that counter is the only thing on the card that mentions the number the trader is being held to. There is no link beside it and no link anywhere on the page back to consignment details (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/animal-identification/_identification-card.njk:9-29). A trader who realises at animal three that they entered two has to leave through "Save and return to hub" or the breadcrumb, find the consignment details row on the hub, and come back. It matters more here than it looks, because Frontend enforces the count in both directions: entering fewer than the line says leaves the section in progress, and reducing the number afterwards is refused outright with "You have N identifier records for X but entered M animals" (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/copy/copy.en.js:38-39).

Design release 1 puts a "Change number of animals" link in the header bar of every species panel, to the right of the species name, pointing at the consignment details page (app/views/animal-identification-details.html:96-98). The correction is one click from the counter that prompted it.

Add a link to the consignment details page in each identification card's heading area, labelled "Change number of animals". The href is the same consignment-details route the hub already links to, so this is a template change in src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/animal-identification/_identification-card.njk with the target passed through the card view model at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/animal-identification/card/view-model.js. increments.title: Frontend counts an animal as identified once one identifier is filled in; Design release 1 does not count it until every identifier for that commodity is filled in
increments.detail:
One identifier is enough. A trader who fills the ear tag and leaves the passport blank presses "Save and add another", the animal is added to the summary list as "Animal 1 — Ear tag: UK123456789012", and the counter moves on. Only an entirely empty animal is refused, with "Enter at least one identifier for this animal" (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/copy/copy.en.js:140), which is the rule the obligation states as a requires-any-of over the six identifier fields (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/commodities/identifiers.js:89-98). fe-animal-identification-saved and fe-animal-identification-at-maximum both show animals saved on an ear tag alone.

Design release 1 appears to require all of them. An animal counts as entered only when every identifier declared for its commodity carries a value (app/routes.js:1526-1532), so a cattle animal needs both an ear tag and a passport. A partly filled animal is not refused and no error is shown — the page simply re-renders the same animal with the values kept and the counter unmoved, and the saved-animals table lists only complete animals. That is a silent outcome rather than a stated rule, which is what makes this finding uncertain.

This is disputed because the two sources of the requirement disagree, and the two readings imply opposite work: if all identifiers are required, Frontend has to change its requires-any-of to a requires-all per commodity and write the error copy for it; if they are not, Frontend is already right and this finding should be struck. Design release 1's behaviour is not in doubt — its entry form holds a trader on an animal until every identifier for that commodity carries a value, and its saved list only ever shows complete animals. What is in doubt is whether that behaviour states a requirement, because the data-fields specification Frontend implements says the opposite in words: the obligation carries the V4 line "Field Block - Mandatory to Submit - At least one Animal Identifier" (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/commodities/identifiers.js:66-72). The one observation that would settle it is a statement from the design authority on which of the two governs — Design release 1's silent per-field behaviour, or the V4 field block. No capture can settle it; see the correction for why the capture originally proposed here cannot fire.

FALSIFIED BY: An error message in Design release 1 naming a missing identifier, or a line in the V4 data-fields specification requiring every identifier for a commodity rather than at least one. Design release 1's identifier validator returns an empty error list unconditionally (app/routes.js:1776-1786), so the design has no way to tell a trader that an identifier is missing.

increments.title: A trader cannot record a microchip number for a dog or a horse anywhere in Frontend; Design release 1 asks for one on both
increments.detail:
Frontend knows six ways to identify an animal and a microchip is not one of them: passport, tattoo, ear tag, horse name, and — only for commodities that have no specific identifier at all — free-text identification details and a description (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/commodities/identifiers.js:113-198). The word microchip appears nowhere in src/server outside a test fixture, where it is typed as a value into the free-text field. The gap bites hardest on the two commodities that need it: because dogs and horses do have specific identifiers, the free-text fallback is switched off for them, so a trader importing a dog is shown a passport and a tattoo field and nothing else. The captured DOM of fe-animal-identification bears this out — the dog line offers animalIdentifierPassport-2 and animalIdentifierTattoo-2, the horse line animalIdentifierPassport-1 and horseName-1, and there is nowhere on the page to put a chip number.

Design release 1 asks for a microchip on both. Its identifiers are declared per commodity code, and a dog (01061900) is asked for Microchip, Passport and Tattoo while a horse (0101) is asked for Microchip, Passport and Horse name (app/data/commodity-identifiers.js:4-17). Microchipping is how a dog is identified in law, so the field is not decoration.

Add a microchip identifier and apply it to the dog and horse commodities. In Frontend that is a seventh obligation beside passport, tattoo, ear tag and horse name in src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/commodities/identifiers.js, an allowlist beside the existing four in src/server/app/sets/live-animals/services/commodities/stub.js:107-115, a label and an error message in src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/copy/copy.en.js:58-72, and its addition to the specific-identifier union so the free-text fallback keeps behaving as it does today. It cannot stop there: the value has to reach the outbox, and the animal identifier record the backend sends to GBNAG recognises only the type codes EAR_TAG and PASSPORT (trade-imports-animals-backend, TradeProductInstance.AnimalIdentifier), so a MICROCHIP type code and the field that feeds it are backend work that has to land alongside.

increments.title: Frontend heads its two identification pages "Animal identification details" and "Additional animal details"; Design release 1 names them "Identification details" and "Additional details"

Each name is used three times on its page — as the h1, as the last breadcrumb and as the browser tab title — so a trader reads it repeatedly. Nothing above either heading says which part of the notification they are in, which is why the heading is carrying the whole burden of orientation.

Design release 1 names the same two pages "Identification details" and "Additional details", and puts the section above them instead: "About the consignment" over the first (app/views/animal-identification-details.html:3, with the caption and heading at :44-47) and "Commodity details" over the second (app/views/additional-animal-details.html:9, caption and heading at :37-38). The caption says what the pages are about, so the heading does not have to, and both names are shorter for it. The same name is used for the page name and the heading in both files.

Rename the two pages to "Identification details" and "Additional details". Each name lives once, in its feature's copy file, and feeds the heading, the breadcrumb and the tab title together, with a Welsh sibling to match. This is one string per page and nothing has to land first. It reads best alongside the section caption, which the service-wide slice owns and which is what makes the shorter names self-explanatory — but it does not depend on it, and the shorter names are the signed-off ones either way.

increments.title: Frontend asks which country the animals will permanently live in; Design release 1 does not ask for a country on the permanent address
increments.detail:
The permanent address block ends with a mandatory "Country" select offering thirty-two countries — the United Kingdom, the EU member states and the rest of the EEA plus Switzerland — under the placeholder "Select a country". increments.title: Frontend makes a trader type the animals' permanent address in full; Design release 1 lets them reuse the place of destination address instead
increments.detail:
On the animal identification page, any animal whose commodity requires a permanent address gets a bare "Permanent address" heading followed by nine empty fields, all of them visible at once. There is no choice to make and nothing to reuse: the trader retypes the name, address, postcode, country, telephone and email for every such animal, even when the animals are going to live at the place of destination they have already given elsewhere in the notification. The block is rendered whenever the commodity requires an address, with nothing gating the fields inside it, at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/animal-identification/_identification-card.njk:43-69, and the nine fields it loops over are fixed at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/animal-identification/address/fields.js:126-163.

Design release 1 asks "Where will their permanent address be?" and offers each animal a two-option radio, "Select an address": "Same as the place of destination (POD)", or "Enter a new address", which opens the address fields as a conditional reveal and is hinted "This is where they will stay after spending 48 hours at the place of destination." Picking the first answers the question in one click, and once a place of destination has been given it is printed as a hint under that option so the trader can see the address they are agreeing to. The two options are built at app/routes.js:2479-2500.

Add a two-option radio above the permanent address fields on the animal identification card — reuse the place of destination address, or enter a new one — and hide the address fields behind the second option. The frontend already collects a place of destination as one of its five consignment parties (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/parties.js:51-55), so the address to copy is in the notification already and nothing outside the frontend has to change. Show the chosen destination address as the hint on the first option, as Design release 1 does, so the trader is not agreeing to an address they cannot see.

FALSIFIED BY: A radio, checkbox or "same as" link anywhere in the frontend's permanent address block that copies an address the trader has already given. The captured DOM of fe-animal-identification contains no input of type radio or checkbox at all.

increments.title: Frontend reads a saved animal back as one run-together line labelled "Animal 1"; Design release 1 reads it back in a table with a column per identifier and the species in the row label
increments.detail:
Once an animal is saved it becomes one row of a summary list above the entry form: a key reading "Animal 1" and a value reading "Ear tag: UK123456789012" — every filled identifier joined into a single sentence with its own label repeated inside it, or the words "No identifier provided" if none were (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/animal-identification/identifier/summary.js:9-18, rendered at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/animal-identification/_identification-card.njk:12-24). There is no header row, so nothing tells a trader which identifiers this commodity expects; a cattle animal saved on an ear tag alone and one saved on both reads as two lines of different lengths and nothing marks which is which. The row is labelled by position rather than by animal — "Animal 1" (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/copy/copy.en.js:87) — so on a page holding four commodity lines the same three words head the first row of every one of them.

Design release 1 reads the same information back as a table underneath the entry form: a header row of "Animal" and then one column per identifier the commodity declares — for cattle, "Ear tag" and "Passport" — then a row per saved animal whose key is the species and its number, "Bos taurus 1", with each identifier in its own cell and a Remove at the end (app/views/partials/animal-identification-saved-animals.html:1-28). Because the columns come from the commodity's own identifier list, a trader can see at a glance which identifiers are expected and which cells are still empty, and the row label says which animal of which species it is.

Replace the summary list of saved animals with a table: a header row naming each identifier the commodity declares, one row per saved animal keyed by species and number, one cell per identifier, and the existing Remove in the last cell. The identifier labels are already in the copy file the header row needs (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/copy/copy.en.js:48-55) and the card view model already knows which identifiers apply to the line, so this is a template and view-model change with no new data. increments.title: Design release 1 asks the purpose and exit questions as conditional reveals under the import reason the user has just chosen; Frontend hides them until the next page and asks each one on a page of its own.
increments.detail:
Choosing an import reason reveals nothing. The captured screenshot of fe-import-reason-transit-selected shows Transit selected and the next thing on the page is the Save and continue button — no port of exit, no destination country. The follow-up questions are separate pages reached only after the user submits, in the fixed order purpose, destination country, port of exit, exit date (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/flow/flow.js:49-57), and the hub carries them as a second, conditional task row of their own (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/flow/task-rows.js:34-39). So Internal market costs a user two page loads, Transhipment or onward travel two, Transit three and Temporary admission horses three, where Design release 1 costs one. Two further differences travel with the split and disappear with it. First, each of the split-out pages says its own name three times — breadcrumb, page heading and field label — so fe-destination-country reads "Destination country / Destination country / Destination country" down the left of the page, from src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/destination-country/template.njk:8 and :16; fe-port-of-exit and fe-exit-date are the same shape. Second, each carries hint text that Design release 1's reveal does not: "The country the consignment travels on to after Great Britain." (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/destination-country/copy/copy.en.js:5) and the leading sentence of "The date the animals are expected to leave Great Britain. For example, 27/3/2026" (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/exit-date/copy/copy.en.js:5) — text a field only needs once it has been stranded on a page with no surrounding question. Both reasons that ask two questions ask them in the opposite order to Design release 1's: Transit asks destination country and then port of exit, and Temporary admission horses asks port of exit and then exit date, because the four pages sit in one fixed sequence and every reason walks the same sequence.

The reason page answers itself. Each importReason radio that has follow-up questions opens them inline underneath it as a conditional reveal, so the user reads the reason, chooses it, answers what it needs and presses Save and continue once (app/views/reason-for-import.html:47-62). Internal market opens the "Purpose in the internal market" question with its eleven radios; Transhipment or onward travel opens a Destination country select; Transit opens Port of exit and then Destination country; Temporary admission horses opens Exit date and then Port of exit; Re-entry opens nothing. No reveal carries a page heading, and only two of them carry any text beyond a field label: the internal-market reveal heads its radios with a medium fieldset legend reading "Purpose in the internal market", and the exit date carries the worked example "For example, 27/3/2026". The other three fields are a bare label over a select, because the radio's own hint above them already supplies the context.

Move the four questions onto the reason page as conditional reveals under the radio that requires them, and delete the four pages, the conditional exit-details task row and the four page-name headings that go with them. Nothing has to land first: the two sides already agree exactly on when each question applies, so no obligation changes. src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/import-reason.js gates purposeInInternalMarket on internalMarket (:43-56), destinationCountry on transit or transhipmentOrOnwardTravel (:66-79), portOfExit on transit or temporaryAdmissionHorses (:86-99) and exitDate on temporaryAdmissionHorses (:103-116), and Design release 1 reveals exactly the same four sets. Take each reveal's internal order from Design release 1 — port of exit then destination country under Transit, and exit date then port of exit under Temporary admission horses. Once the questions sit under their radio, drop the destination-country hint and the leading sentence of the exit-date hint, keeping the worked example "For example, 27/3/2026" that Design release 1 also shows.

increments.title: Frontend lets a user pick any port of entry as the port of exit; Design release 1 offers only the border control posts approved for animals leaving Great Britain.
increments.detail:
The port-of-exit select is the port-of-entry list. Its captured DOM offers about eighty entries running from "Aberdeen Airport (GB DYC)" to the far end of the alphabet, including inland and cargo terminals such as "Nottingham Port (GB NTG)" and "HES Humber Bulk Terminal (GB HMR)", and the page says so out loud: the field's hint reads "Choose where the consignment will leave Great Britain. Exit and entry share the same port list." (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/port-of-exit/copy/copy.en.js:5). This is a design decision rather than fixture contents. The controller builds the options by mapping the single shared ports service (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/port-of-exit/controller.js:22-29) and validates the answer against that same list (:32-38); the service holds one list and primes it from the reference-data service's ports-of-entry endpoint (src/server/app/services/ports/client.js:4-6). There is no exit list and no filter over the entry list. The frontend's own obligation records where the decision came from: "Port selected from the port of entry list (Exit and Entry share the same list)" at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/import-reason.js:81-83.

The port of exit is a short, purpose-built list of ten border control posts approved to handle animals: Edinburgh, Gatwick, Glasgow, three Heathrow posts, Holyhead, Manchester, Prestwick and Stansted, each carrying its BCP code. Design release 1 keeps it in its own file, separate from the arrival ports, and names it for what it is (app/data/exit-border-control-posts.js:1-14). Both reveals that ask for a port of exit use it — the transit reveal, where the field is named transitExitBorderControlPost, and the temporary-admission reveal, where it is named temporaryAdmissionPortOfExit — and both are fed by the same builder at app/routes.js:8763-8776. The user is offered no other option.

The port of exit has to become its own list of animal exit border control posts rather than a second use of the arrival ports. Frontend cannot do this alone: the ports service exposes one list and the reference-data service exposes only ports-of-entry, so a new endpoint and a new reference list are needed in trade-imports-reference-data, and the ports service needs a second accessor beside list(). Once that exists the frontend change is small — a different source for portItems and for the validation set in the same controller, and the hint sentence "Exit and entry share the same port list." comes out. Note for whoever schedules this: Frontend is not doing this by accident. It is following a different requirements source, the V4 field spec quoted in its own obligation, which says exit and entry share a list. Design release 1 is the signed-off design and says otherwise, so the two documents disagree and this ticket is where that gets settled.

FALSIFIED BY: A second port list in the frontend, or an exit filter over the one it has. src/server/app/services/ports/index.js exposes exactly one list, primed from one endpoint, and the port-of-exit select maps over it unfiltered; finding an exit-specific source would prove this wrong.

increments.title: Frontend lets a user leave the internal-market purpose and the exit date blank and carry on; Design release 1 keeps them on the page with an error until they are answered.
increments.detail:
A user who chooses Internal market, reaches the purpose page, selects nothing and presses Save and continue is taken to the next page. The same happens on the exit-date page: leave the box empty, press Save and continue, and the journey moves on. Neither page has an error message to show, and neither copy file carries one for a blank answer — the purpose page validates with oneOf, which treats an empty string as a valid choice (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/import-purpose/controller.js:25-30, and the validator itself at src/server/app/lib/validate/validators.js:114-121), and the exit-date page validates with dateText, which allows an empty string through before it ever tries to read a date (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/exit-date/controller.js:21 and src/server/app/lib/validate/validators.js:209-234). The two remaining exit questions do stop the user: destination country and port of exit both use requiredOneOf and both produce an error, which the captured screens fe-destination-country-error and fe-port-of-exit-error show. The notification is not submittable in this state — purposeInInternalMarket and exitDate are mandatory once in scope (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/import-reason.js:43-56 and :103-116), and the review section is gated on every task row being fulfilled, not applicable or optional (src/server/app/flow/section-status.js:11-15, applied at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/flow/flow.js:81-85, the gate itself at :83). So this is not a hole a user can submit through: it is a user who is let past the question and told nothing, and who finds out only when the check-answers step will not open.

Choosing a reason and leaving its revealed question blank returns the user to the same page with an error summary and an error against the field. Design release 1 says which message goes with which gap: "Select a purpose in the internal market" under Internal market, "Enter an exit date" for an empty exit date and "Enter a real date" for one it cannot read, "Select a destination country" and "Select a port of exit" (app/routes.js:1387-1441). The main reason itself is deliberately not enforced — the design states in its own words that "a main reason is optional to proceed, but once selected any further information required for that reason must be completed" (app/routes.js:1381-1385) — so the two sides already agree about the reason radio and disagree only about what hangs off it.

Make purposeInInternalMarket and exitDate required at the point they are asked, so a blank answer returns the page with an error summary rather than advancing. On the purpose page swap oneOf for requiredOneOf and add the message "Select a purpose in the internal market" to src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/import-purpose/copy/copy.en.js, which today has no errors block at all; on the exit-date page add a required check ahead of the date parse with the message "Enter an exit date". Do not make the reason radio required — Design release 1 lets a user leave it blank and Frontend already matches that. Nothing has to land first; the obligation model already marks both fields mandatory, so this only moves the moment the user is told. If import-reason--exit-questions-split-onto-separate-pages lands first, the same two checks belong on the reveals instead of on two pages that will no longer exist.

increments.detail:
The eleven purpose options and their order match Design release 1 exactly, but four of the hints beneath them do not. Three more end without a full stop: "... or produce offspring", "Animals to participate in competitive or training events" and "... any other animal product or by-product". All four come from src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/import-purpose/copy/copy.en.js:6, :10, :13 and :19. The other seven hints match word for word.

Design release 1 writes the same four hints in plain, correct English and closes every one of them with a full stop: "Any movement of an animal that has as its aim the sale of or the transfer of ownership of the animal ... with no sale involved (for example a gift).", "... or produce offspring.", "Animals to participate in competitive or training events." and "... any other animal product or by-product." (app/data/internal-market-purposes.js:7, :17, :27, :42).

Replace those four hint strings in the frontend's import-purpose copy with Design release 1's wording: fix "it's" to "its", drop the comma after "aim", spell "e.g." out as "for example", and add the missing full stop to all four. One file, four strings, nothing has to land first. Do the Welsh file in the same pass if the same drift is in it.

increments.title: Frontend collects the country of origin from a dropdown list; Design release 1 asks the user to search for it.
increments.detail:
The origin page offers a standard GOV.UK select about a third of the content width, whose first option reads "Select a country" and whose second is a disabled row of dashes acting as a separator. The user opens the list and scrolls it to find the country; there is no way to type. The control is declared at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/origin/template.njk:15-22 and its options are assembled at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/origin/controller.js:57-61.

The origin page offers a full-width search box with a magnifying-glass button and the placeholder "Search for a country". Typing filters a results list that opens underneath it, and picking a result leaves the country's name in the box and records the choice behind it — the captured picture of the revealed state shows "France" sitting in the search box. The control is declared at app/views/origin-of-the-import.html:55-97.

Replace the country select on the origin page with a search-and-pick control: a full-width search input labelled as now, a results list that filters as the user types, and the chosen country left visible in the box. The countries themselves do not change — both sides read a list and this finding is about how the user reaches an entry in it, not about which entries there are. The country the user picks also has to be readable by the region-of-origin code field, which is the separate finding origin--region-code-country-prefix; build the picker so that choosing a country can drive that prefix. Nothing has to land before this: the country list is already in Frontend's countries service.

increments.title: Design release 1 fills in the country's code as a fixed prefix and asks only for the rest of the region of origin code; Frontend makes the user type the whole code inside five characters.
increments.detail:
Answering Yes reveals one plain text box, five characters wide, labelled "Region of origin code" and hinted "For example, FR-75". The user types the whole code including the country part, and the whole value is capped at five characters (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/origin/controller.js:71-75). For a consignment from France that leaves two characters for the region once "FR-" has been typed, so any region whose code runs longer than two characters cannot be entered at all. The field is declared at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/origin/template.njk:24-34.

Answering Yes reveals a field labelled "Enter the region of origin code", hinted "Enter up to 5 characters.", made of two parts: a grey, unfocusable prefix box already showing the two-letter code of the country chosen higher up the page — "FR" in the captured picture — and a text box beside it. The user types only the part after the prefix and has all five characters for it; the service joins the two into the full code. The field is declared at app/views/partials/region-of-origin-code-input.html:14-29 and revealed from app/views/origin-of-the-import.html:102.

On the origin page, derive the prefix from the country the user has already chosen, render it as a govuk-input prefix beside the code box, and collect and validate only the part after it, up to five characters. Relabel the field "Enter the region of origin code" and replace the worked example with "Enter up to 5 characters.". Frontend already holds the two-letter code as the value of every country option (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/origin/controller.js:57-61), so no new reference data is needed for the countries it lists; Design release 1's own prefix map departs from the plain country code only for Ceuta and Melilla, neither of which is in Frontend's list. Moving the five-character cap from the whole code to the part after the prefix is the substance of the change, and it is what makes longer regional codes enterable. Design release 1 also upper-cases what the user typed and joins the two parts with a hyphen, so typing "75" with France chosen records "FR-75" (app/routes.js:9239, :9246-9251); Frontend only trims the box, so build the same normalisation in.

increments.title: Frontend lets a user answer Yes to the region of origin question and continue with the code box left empty; Design release 1 holds them on the page until they enter it.
increments.detail:
The revealed code box is checked for length and nothing else. The origin page's rule set requires a country, accepts either answer to the region question, and applies a maximum-length rule to the code and two rules to the internal reference — there is no presence rule for the code at all (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/origin/controller.js:63-82). So a user can select Yes, leave the box empty, press Save and continue, and reach the next page having recorded no region of origin code. The page is perfectly able to show an error — fe-origin-error is the same page holding a user back for a missing country — so this is a missing rule rather than a missing mechanism.

Submitting the origin page with Yes selected and the code box empty re-renders the page with "Enter the region of origin code" in the error summary, linked to the code field. It is the only rule Design release 1 states for this page (app/routes.js:254-260).

Add a presence rule to the region of origin code that fires only when the region question is answered Yes, with the message "Enter the region of origin code", and add that message to the origin feature's copy alongside the length message already there (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/origin/copy/copy.en.js:21-26). Nothing has to land first. Design release 1's origin page was not photographed in its error state, so the observation that would settle the wording and the anchor is that page submitted with Yes chosen and the code box empty. The obligation behind the field is already right and must not be touched: it is marked mandatory whenever the requirement is Yes (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/origin.js:27-36), which is why the notification cannot be submitted with the box empty. All that is missing is the page-level rule that tells the user so at the point of the mistake.

FALSIFIED BY: Submitting fe-origin with Yes selected and the code box empty and being held on the page with an error. Frontend's origin validator composes exactly one required rule (for the country), one either-or rule for the radio and two maximum-length rules, so the code's presence is never checked; a page that refused that submission would prove this wrong.

What the finding says is true of the page: the user answers Yes, leaves the box empty, presses Save and continue and moves on. What it does not say is that the journey does stop them later. regionOfOriginCode is already marked mandatory whenever the requirement is Yes (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/origin.js:27-36, an equalsGate on regionCodeRequirement), so the origin task row can never reach Fulfilled while the box is empty (src/server/app/bridge/status/index.js:68-76 returns IN_PROGRESS), readyForCheckYourAnswers stays false (src/server/app/flow/section-status.js:11-15), the review section gate refuses (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/flow/flow.js:83) and the submit itself refuses (src/server/app/engine/write/submit.js:9). increments.title: The review page calls the arrival date "Arrival date at port of entry" where Design release 1 calls it "Arrival date at destination" — but Design release 1's own question page calls it "at port of entry", so the two releases of that label disagree inside Design release 1
increments.detail:
The Arrival details card on Check your answers labels the row "Arrival date at port of entry" (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/check-answers/copy/copy.en.js:70), the same words the question page uses when it asks for the answer (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/transport/copy/copy.en.js:5). Question and summary agree.

Design release 1 labels the same value two different ways on two of its own screens. Its arrival-details question asks for "Arrival date at port of entry" (app/views/partials/arrival-date-picker.html:9), storing the answer as `arrivalDateAtPort`; its review page then prints that same stored value under the key "Arrival date at destination" (app/routes.js:4676-4679), and its dashboard cards use "Arrival date at destination" too. A port of entry and a place of destination are two different places in this service — the notification collects an address for each — so the two labels do not describe the same thing, and only one of them can be right.

Nothing should change until somebody says which label Design release 1 means. This is banded disputed because Design release 1 contradicts itself between two of its own screens rather than because the frontend might be wrong. The observation that settles it is a ruling on whether the date being collected is the arrival at the port of entry or the arrival at the place of destination. If it is the port of entry, Design release 1's review and dashboard labels are the mistake and the frontend is already right. If it is the destination, then both sides' question pages are mislabelled as well as the frontend's review row, and the change is much wider than this one string.

increments.title: Check your answers puts a Change link on every row, so a finished notification offers twenty-four of them; Design release 1 puts one Change link in each card's heading and none on the rows
increments.detail:
Every row of every card carries its own Change link on the right-hand side. A finished notification shows twenty-four of them — twenty-two on rows, plus two in the heading of the Species card, which is the only card on the page with card-level actions. An unfinished notification shows eighteen, all on rows. Each link goes to the page that collects that one answer, with a `change=1` flag so the trader is returned to the review afterwards (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/check-answers/view-model/rows/summary-row.js:14-21, building the action at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/check-answers/view-model/rows/change-link.js:12-25). So the page repeats the same destination link once per row: five rows in the Arrival details card all lead to the arrival details page, five in Roles and addresses all lead to the roles and addresses page.

Design release 1 puts one Change link in each card's heading bar, level with the card title, and no link on any row (app/views/partials/review-summary-card.html:23-28 renders the single title link from the card's own changeHref, and app/views/partials/review-summary-row.html:14-24 renders a row as a key and a value with no action at all). Both the finished and the unfinished review page carry exactly eleven Change links, one per card, each going to the page that collects that card's answers.

Move the Change link from the row to the card. Give each card in the check-answers view-model one action, pointing at the page that collects that card's answers, and stop attaching a change action to individual rows — that is `summary-row.js` dropping its call to `changeAction`, and each card builder gaining the card-level action the Species card already has. The visually hidden text moves with it, from naming the row to naming the card. Nothing has to land first, and the destinations do not change: every row in a card already resolves to the same page, so no route is lost. `controls` is deliberately empty for two reasons: the finding is the arrangement of the whole page rather than any one field, and "Change" lands twenty-four times on the frontend page, so naming it would get the crop refused and fall back to the whole-page shot anyway.

increments.title: The declaration states three bare headings where Design release 1 states each one and then explains what it commits the trader to
increments.detail:
The page is three headings, a four-item list and two closing sentences, with no supporting text under any heading (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/declaration/copy/copy.en.js:3-18). The first heading, "I am the contact for the authorities and located in the UK.", stands alone. The second is a single long heading, "I confirm I am responsible for this consignment until it has cleared border control checks or reached the place of destination." The accountability list reads "payments for border control checks", "re-dispatch of the consignment", "quarantine or isolation of the animals", "the costs of destruction and disposal". So a trader ticking the box is agreeing to four compressed phrases with no statement of when the responsibility starts or which regulation it sits under.

Design release 1 gives each statement a heading and a body (app/views/declaration.html:40-64). "I am the contact for the authorities and located in the UK." is followed by "I am complying with the requirements of Regulation (EU) 2017/625 including on animal health and welfare." "I confirm I am responsible for this consignment." is followed by "I am responsible from the submission of this notification to when it enters Great Britain. And I am responsible until it has either:" and two bullets, "cleared official checks at the border" and "reached the Place of Destination as stated on the health certificate or notification". The accountability list reads "any payment for the official controls at the border", "any arrangements to re-dispatch the consignment", "any costs needed for quarantine or isolation of consignments", "any costs needed for destruction and disposal of consignments, when instructed by the authorities". The two closing sentences are the same on both sides, and so is the checkbox label.

Replace the declaration body copy with Design release 1's wording: add the Regulation (EU) 2017/625 sentence under the first heading; shorten the second heading to "I confirm I am responsible for this consignment." and add the sentence and two bullets beneath it; and reword the four accountability items. This is a copy change in src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/declaration/copy/copy.en.js plus the small template change needed to render a paragraph and a nested list under the first two headings. `controls` is deliberately empty: the finding is the body of the declaration, which is prose rather than any one control, and the checkbox beneath it is word-for-word identical on both sides.

increments.title: Deleting a notification and cancelling an amendment are frontend journeys Design release 1 does not describe at all
increments.detail:
Two confirmation pages exist that have no counterpart. "Delete this notification?" warns "This cannot be undone." and offers "Yes, delete notification" against "No, return to dashboard"; it is reached from the Delete action on a dashboard card and from the Delete button on a submitted notification's review page. "Cancel this amendment?" warns "Your changes since you started amending will be discarded and the submitted version restored." and offers "Yes, cancel amendment" against "No, return to notification"; it is reachable only from a notification the trader has put into the amending state, which the frontend's dashboard offers on a submitted notification and Design release 1's does not.

Design release 1 has neither page and neither journey. Both routes exist on the prototype's single router, but neither reaches this release: the delete page redirects to the dashboard unless a Design release 2 session flag is set (app/routes.js:5607-5613), the cancel-amendment handler does the same, and neither has a root view — there is no delete-notification.html and no cancel-amend.html at the root of app/views, only copies under design-release-2/ and design-release-2.1/, which are other releases' documents. Design release 1's dashboard cards offer "Copy as new" and "View" and no delete or amend action at all, so neither journey has a way in.

This is recorded once as a one-sided observation and needs no work: Design release 1 says nothing about deleting a notification or amending a submitted one, so it cannot be said to disagree with the frontend having them. It is banded disputed because the one thing this comparison cannot settle is whether the silence is deliberate — whether these two journeys were designed elsewhere and are correct, or were built ahead of the design. The observation that would settle it is a signed-off Design release 1 artefact, outside the prototype's root views, that either specifies or rules out deleting a notification and amending a submitted one. Until somebody produces that, no change should be made on either side. The frontend states are recorded in this corpus so a person can look at them: fe-delete-notification, fe-cancel-amend, and fe-dashboard-deleted for what the dashboard shows afterwards.

increments.title: Check your answers gives no sign that a notification is incomplete; Design release 1 heads the review page with "There is a problem", names each unfinished section and refuses to go on
increments.detail:
A trader who reaches Check your answers before the notification is finished sees a page that looks finished. Every unanswered row reads "Not provided" in ordinary black text, no card is marked, there is no error summary, and the page still ends with the heading "Now submit your notification", the sentence "Continue to the declaration to submit your notification." and a green Continue button (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/check-answers/template.njk:108-114). Nothing on the page says what is outstanding or where to go to finish it. Pressing Continue is not refused either: the POST handler redirects straight on to the declaration (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/check-answers/controller.js:96-99), the declaration renders, and only after the trader ticks the box and presses Continue again does the submit fail its readiness check and bounce back to Check your answers with no message at all (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/declaration/controller.js:86-88, src/server/app/engine/write/submit.js:9-15). The trader ends up back where they started having been told nothing.

Design release 1's review page opens with a red-bordered "There is a problem" summary carrying one link per unfinished card — "Complete arrival details", "Complete transport details", "Complete roles and addresses", "Complete contact address for this consignment" — each anchored to the card it names (app/views/review-notification.html:29-36). Every unfinished card is drawn with a red left bar and repeats its own message in red inside the card, and each of its rows is blank rather than filled with a placeholder. Continue does not move on: the POST re-renders the same page with the same summary until the notification is complete.

Give Check your answers the incomplete state Design release 1 shows. On render, work out which cards are unfinished and put an error summary above the heading listing one "Complete <card name>" link per unfinished card, anchored to that card; mark each unfinished card with its own inline error message; and make the POST re-render the page rather than continue to the declaration when the notification is not ready. The readiness signal already exists — `scope.readyForCheckYourAnswers` — and the per-card breakdown can come from the same task-row statuses the hub uses (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/flow/task-rows.js). Nothing has to land first. `controls` is deliberately empty: the finding is the state of the whole page, not one field, and a crop of any single row would hide the error summary that is the substance of it.

increments.title: Check your answers prints "Not provided" both for a question that does not apply and for an answer that is still needed; Design release 1 says "Not applicable" for the first and marks the second as missing
increments.detail:
One string stands in for every empty value. On the complete notification, "Region of origin code" and "Internal reference number" both read "Not provided" — and both are questions that genuinely do not apply, because the trader answered No to the region-code question and the internal reference is optional. On the unfinished notification, "Port of entry" also reads "Not provided" — and that one is required before the notification can be submitted. The two states are typeset identically, so a trader reading the page cannot tell which rows are finished business and which are work still to do. The single string comes from `notProvided` in src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/check-answers/copy/copy.en.js:3, applied to every blank value at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/check-answers/view-model/rows/value-text.js:11-13.

Design release 1 has two different treatments. A value that does not apply is written out as "Not applicable" (app/routes.js:4065-4071) — that is what its review page shows against "Region of origin code" and "Internal reference number". A value that is required and absent is not given text at all: the row is drawn in the missing style with only a visually hidden "Missing" for a screen reader (app/views/partials/review-summary-row.html:15-21), inside a card that is itself marked with an error. So on Design release 1 the eye can separate "nothing needed here" from "something still owed here" without reading a word.

Split the one placeholder into two, and follow Design release 1 in deciding per card rather than per row. In a card that is complete, print "Not applicable" for every empty value. In a card that is unfinished — the same cards that would carry the inline error from review--incomplete-notification-not-flagged-on-check-answers — print no placeholder text at all: draw every empty row in a missing style with only a visually hidden "Missing", whether that particular row was required or optional. The frontend already knows which cards are unfinished, because the same task-row statuses drive the hub, so this is a rendering change in the check-answers view-model with nothing to land first.

increments.title: After submitting, the frontend never tells the trader what is still outstanding; Design release 1 heads the submitted page with "Before the consignment is imported" and lists the documents and identifiers still owed
increments.detail:
The confirmation page goes straight from the green panel to "Transporting the consignment" (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/confirmation/template.njk:4-13). There is no section about work still to do. This matters because the frontend does accept a submission with no documents at all: the documents group carries neither a minimum entry count nor a required-one-of rule (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/documents.js:19-27), so an untouched documents collection rolls up as optional and the readiness check passes without it. A trader can therefore submit a notification with no health certificate attached, reach a page headed "Import notification submitted", and be told nothing about the certificate.

Design release 1 puts a section between the panel and the transport guidance whenever anything is still outstanding: "Before the consignment is imported", the line "You still need to:", and a bulleted list (app/views/notification-submitted.html:27-36). The two items it can carry are "upload the health certificate and any other required documents", shown whenever no document has been uploaded, and "complete the animal identifier information in the notification", shown when identifiers were allowed through the submit gate but are not yet complete (app/routes.js:5674-5692). The section disappears entirely when nothing is outstanding.

Add the same section to the confirmation page: a heading "Before the consignment is imported", the line "You still need to:", and one bullet per outstanding item, rendered only when there is at least one. The documents bullet can be built today and nothing has to land first: documents are optional for submission, so the frontend can reach this page with an empty collection, and it already knows that at submit time. The identifier bullet cannot fire today and should not be built until the identifier question is settled — the frontend's submit gate requires one animal-identifier record per animal (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/commodities/identifiers.js:88-102 sets recordCountEquals against numberOfAnimals) and readiness requires every task row to be fulfilled (src/server/app/flow/section-status.js:11-15), so a notification with animals still to identify never reaches the confirmation page at all. Design release 1 does let one through, which is why it has that bullet. Whether a partly identified animal counts as outstanding is the open question in identification--identifier-completeness; build the identifier bullet with whatever answer that finding gets.

increments.title: Frontend will not accept a notification until every animal has been identified; Design release 1 accepts one with no identifiers at all and asks for them after submission
increments.detail:
A trader cannot submit until every animal on every commodity line has an identifier record. The animal-identifier group carries a count rule as well as a content rule: each unit record must hold at least one of the six identifiers, and the number of unit records on a commodity line must equal the number of animals declared for that line (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/commodities/identifiers.js:98-101, `recordCountEquals` against `numberOfAnimals`). That group is the whole of the `animalIdentification` task row (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/flow/task-rows.js:41-45), and readiness demands every task row be fulfilled, not applicable or optional (src/server/app/flow/section-status.js:11-15). Readiness is the gate on both the review section (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/flow/flow.js:81-85) and the submit itself, which returns `ok: false` and goes nowhere without it (src/server/app/engine/write/submit.js:9-15). So a trader who declares twenty animals must fill in twenty identifier cards before the service will take the notification. Documents are the one thing Frontend does let through: the documents group carries no minimum, so an empty collection is not a bar.

Design release 1 asks for none of it. Its submit gate ends with the line "Documents remain optional. Animal identifiers are optional unless multiple species are selected, in which case at least one identifier is required per species" (app/routes.js:4562-4566). The minimum returns true outright for a single-species consignment however many identifier fields that commodity carries, and for a multi-species one it asks for a single complete entry per species, never one per animal (app/routes.js:1511-1523). The captured review page is the proof: a notification of five Bison bison with no identifier saved shows an empty "Bison Bison" card under "Identification details", no error summary, and a live Continue button. Design release 1 then chases what is missing rather than refusing it — the submitted page carries "You still need to:" with "complete the animal identifier information in the notification" as a bullet.

Move the animal-identifier requirement out of the submit gate and into the follow-up. Concretely: keep the per-record rule that a saved animal must carry at least one identifier, but stop the `animalIdentification` task row blocking readiness — drop `recordCountEquals` from the unit-record obligation's `requires` (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/commodities/identifiers.js:98-101) so an under-identified line no longer holds the row out of FULFILLED, and let the row roll up as optional the way documents already do. The count itself is still worth showing on the hub and on Check your answers as progress; it just must not stop a submission. Then say what is outstanding after submission, which is the work in review--no-outstanding-tasks-after-submitting; that finding parks its identifier bullet because the frontend cannot currently reach the confirmation page with animals unidentified, and this change is what unparks it. Nothing has to land first: the obligation, the task row and the readiness roll-up are all frontend files, and the animals backend's submit transition rejects a notification only on its status, never on its content, so no contract or API change is needed to accept a partly identified one.

FALSIFIED BY: An animal-identifier entry in Design release 1's review-page error summary on a single-species notification with no identifiers saved. The captured dr1-review-notification-incomplete lists exactly four problems — "Complete arrival details", "Complete transport details", "Complete roles and addresses", "Complete contact address for this consignment" — and no identifier among them, on a notification that had saved none.

This finding exists because a corpus-wide sweep found that nobody had raised it: the difference is named in slices.json as the review slice's central one, and it survived in the 115 only as supporting context inside review--no-outstanding-tasks-after-submitting, where it is used as the reason that finding's identifier bullet cannot be built. It was written, and checked, by the same agent, and it has had no independent verifier. What was checked: ran the falsifier over capture/html/prototype/dr1-review-notification-incomplete.html — four error-summary links, none about identifiers — and over capture/html/prototype/dr1-review-notification.html, which has no govuk-error-summary at all. Traced both gates in source rather than inferring them: on the requirements side app/routes.js:4529-4569 is the ten-predicate run and app/routes.js:10068-10074 is the POST that re-renders on failure; on the implementation side the four frontend citations were each opened and the ranges are exact. Checked the band by reading the animals backend's submitNotification, which throws only when the status is not DRAFT or AMEND and never inspects content — so this is frontend-work, not needs-backend. relatedTo.why: That finding adds the outstanding-work section to the confirmation page but parks its identifier bullet because the frontend cannot reach that page with animals unidentified; this finding is what makes the bullet reachable, so the two are one change in two halves.

Both are about how much identification the service demands, but they ask different questions: that one is how many of an animal's identifiers must be filled in before the animal counts as entered, this one is how many animals must be entered before the notification can be submitted. Whatever answer that dispute gets applies to the per-record rule this finding deliberately keeps.

That finding is about how the gate is presented when it fires; this one is about what the gate contains. Changing the contents without adding the presentation would leave a trader still blocked silently by the remaining rows.

increments.title: The read-only view of an already-submitted notification still ends with "Now submit your notification" and a Continue button; Design release 1 renders no form once a notification is submitted
increments.detail:
When a notification has been submitted, the review page is redrawn read-only: the status tag turns green and reads "Submitted", every Change link is removed, and "Copy as new" and "Delete" buttons appear at the top. But the foot of the page is unchanged. It still carries the heading "Now submit your notification", the sentence "Continue to the declaration to submit your notification." and a green Continue button (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/check-answers/template.njk:108-114, which is outside every read-only branch on the page). So a page that has just told the trader the notification is submitted, and that has removed every other way of changing it, invites them to submit it again.

Design release 1 wraps the whole form in a read-only test and renders nothing at the foot of the page for a submitted notification (app/views/review-notification.html:180-186). The read-only review ends with the last card. This half is read from the view rather than from a picture: Design release 1 captured no submitted review, so the prototype screen in this pair is its draft review. The state that would show it is a Design release 1 review page reached with a `submitted` query parameter, which is the only way that side renders read-only (app/routes.js:10026-10037).

Suppress the submit block — heading, sentence and Continue button — when the review is read-only. increments.title: The dashboard shows no "At a glance" summary; Design release 1 opens it with counts of alerts, errors and messages waiting for the trader
increments.detail:
The dashboard goes straight from the start button to "Your notifications" and the list (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/dashboard/template.njk:27-56). There is nothing above the list summarising what needs the trader's attention, and no alerts, errors or messages anywhere in the service — the words appear in none of the 67 captured frontend screens. A trader with a notification the authorities have rejected learns it only by reading the status tag on that notification's card.

Between the start button and the notification list Design release 1 shows a section headed "At a glance" holding three cards side by side: Alerts, Errors and Messages (app/views/dashboard.html:39-77). Each card shows an icon, a count, and a link — "View alerts", "View errors", "View messages" — that takes the trader to the detail. The counts come from the view model's alertCounts and read 0 in the capture. The links are placeholders in the prototype, so the design states that the three lists exist and are reachable but not what they contain.

Add a summary section to the dashboard above the notification list, headed "At a glance", with a card per category showing the count and a link through to it. Three things have to exist before it is more than decoration: a source of alert, error and message counts for the signed-in organisation, which no service in this workspace exposes today and which the notification contract does not carry; a decision on what an alert, an error and a message are, since Design release 1 shows the categories and not their contents; and the three destination pages the links point at, which Design release 1 leaves as placeholders. The section itself can be built and shown with zero counts before any of that lands, so the visual work does not have to wait, but the section is not worth shipping until the counts are real.

increments.title: A dashboard card's links change with the notification's status and a draft can only be resumed, never viewed; Design release 1 gives every card the same two links, Copy as new and View
increments.detail:
Each card's link row is built from the notification's status, so a trader meets a different set on different cards (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/dashboard/view-model/row/actions.js:18-67). A draft gets Resume, Copy as new and Delete; a submitted notification gets View, Amend, Copy as new and Delete; one being amended gets Resume, Copy as new, Cancel amendment and Delete. The captured draft cards show exactly three links — Resume, Copy as new, Delete. There is no way to look at a draft without re-entering it: Resume goes to the task list (`hubPath`) and View exists only once the notification has been submitted, when it opens Check your answers.

Design release 1 gives every card the same two links whatever its status, side by side after the reference and separated by a divider: "Copy as new" and "View" (app/views/dashboard.html:258-262, which carries no status condition of any kind). The captured dashboard shows four cards — two "Submitted", two "Submitted action required" — and all four carry that identical pair. Design release 1 offers no Resume, no Delete, no Amend and no Cancel amendment on a card, and its View is the way into a draft as much as into a submitted one: for a draft the link is built as `/review-notification?reference=…` and for a submitted one as `/review-notification?submitted=…`, so both open the review page and a trader continues a draft by following the Change links from there.

Make the card's link row fixed rather than status-driven, and offer View on every card. In src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/dashboard/view-model/row/actions.js:18-67 the three status branches collapse to one list; "View" replaces "Resume" as the label on a draft and points at Check your answers, the same target it already uses on a submitted notification, which makes the read-only view reachable for a draft for the first time. The order the design shows is Copy as new then View, which is the reverse of the frontend's current copy-then-open order for a draft. Two things are deliberately outside this finding. Delete, Amend and Cancel amendment are the frontend-only journeys already recorded in review--deleting-and-cancelling-an-amendment-are-one-sided, where they are banded disputed pending an artefact that either specifies or rules them out; do not strip those links on the strength of this finding. And whether the frontend should keep a separate route back into a half-finished draft's task list is a question about the hub, not about the card — Design release 1 does not offer one, and if the answer is that it should be kept then it is a third link beside these two, not a replacement for View.

FALSIFIED BY: A status condition around the action block in Design release 1's dashboard card, or a card in the captured dr1-dashboard carrying anything other than Copy as new and View. Extracting every `app-dashboard-notification-card__action` from capture/html/prototype/dr1-dashboard.html gives eight links across four cards, alternating "Copy as new" and "View" and nothing else.

increments.title: The dashboard can only be filtered by keyword; Design release 1 also filters by commodity, consignee, status and a date range
increments.detail:
The filter panel beside the notification list holds one field, "Keyword or reference", and a "Search" button (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/dashboard/template.njk:38-56). Submitting it sets a referenceNumber query parameter, which is the only filter the dashboard controller reads (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/dashboard/controller.js:54-59). A trader with a long list cannot narrow it to one commodity, one consignee, one status or one week.

Design release 1's panel is labelled "Filter notifications" and holds three collapsible sections (app/views/dashboard.html:83-228). "Search by" holds three text fields: "Keyword or notification number", "Commodity code or name" and "Consignee/Importer". "Status" holds a select offering Draft, Submitted, In progress, Approved, Action required, Rejected and Complete. "By date" holds a radio group of Today, Tomorrow and Next seven days, then a "Select date range" pair of date pickers labelled "Start date" and "End date" under the hint "For example, 27/3/2026". The three sections are closed when the page loads and none carries a submit button of its own.

Build the panel as three collapsible sections and add the filters the design lists: commodity, consignee, status and a date range with the three shortcut radios. The design does not say which date the range filters on — the section is headed "By date", its visually hidden legend reads "Choose a date range" and the fields are "Start date" and "End date" — so that has to be settled before the filter can be applied; the shortcuts Today, Tomorrow and Next seven days point at a future date, which on a notification is the arrival date, but the design does not state it. Rename the existing field to "Keyword or notification number" as the design has it. Each new filter needs the list endpoint to accept and apply it — the persistence layer's list query today takes page, sort and referenceNumber only (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/dashboard/controller.js:54-59) — so the query contract has to grow before any of these can do anything. Take the status list from the notification statuses this service actually has rather than copying the design's seven, which are a fixture; the frontend today renders Draft, Submitted, Amending and Deleted (src/server/app/shared/copy.en.js:47-51), so which set is right is a question for the same conversation. Whether the panel keeps a submit button is recorded separately under service-wide--dashboard-sort-needs-an-update-button.

FALSIFIED BY: Finding a commodity, consignee, status or date field in the captured DOM of any frontend dashboard screen.
