increments.title: Frontend's dashboard always has an ordering applied and no way to have none; Design release 1's sort control loads unselected, so the list starts in whatever order the service returns it
increments.detail:
There is no unsorted state anywhere in the dashboard. Every option in the select names an ordering, and one of them is always in force: the controller parses the sort query parameter and falls back to a default when it is absent or unrecognised (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/dashboard/controller.js:53, through parseNotificationSort at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/dashboard/notification-helper.js:58-60), and the picture of fe-dashboard-populated shows "Arrival (newest to oldest)" already selected on a page the trader has not touched. The default is carried all the way to the notification list read, which defaults the parameter again and interpolates it unconditionally into the request (src/server/app/services/persistence/records/real/lifecycle/read.js:26 and :34). So a trader cannot see the list in the order the service returns it, and the page never has to answer the question of what to show when nothing has been chosen.

Design release 1's select loads on "Select one", an unselected placeholder ahead of its three orderings (app/data/dashboard-notifications.js:147-152), and the captured DOM of dr1-dashboard shows it selected. So the design's starting state is a list with no ordering named. The design does not say what that order should be, and it cannot be read off the prototype: getDashboardViewModel reads the sort parameter, hands it to buildDashboardSortItems so the right option shows as selected and to the pagination hrefs, and never orders the notification list by it (app/routes.js:7138-7255), so the prototype's list is in fixture order whatever the select says.

Give the dashboard a state in which no ordering has been chosen, and decide what the list query does in it. Two things have to happen in Frontend. The sort control needs an unselected entry that is not an ordering, which means the default at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/dashboard/notification-helper.js:58-65 stops being applied when the trader has chosen nothing rather than being applied silently. Then the notification list read has to be able to ask for a page without an ordering: src/server/app/services/persistence/records/real/lifecycle/read.js:26 defaults sort to arrivalDate,desc and :34 puts it in the query string on every call, so the parameter has to become optional there and the stub at src/server/app/services/persistence/records/stub/lifecycle/read.js:18 has to match. The band is frontend-work because both edits are Frontend's and the frontend can build and run this against its own stub today — but confirm with the notifications API's owners what order it returns when no sort parameter is sent before this ships, because that order is what a trader will actually see and neither this design nor the prototype specifies it. Adding the "Select one" label to the options list is part of the copy change raised as service-wide--dashboard-sort-orderings-differ; this finding is what the label has to mean.

FALSIFIED BY: Finding a request from Frontend's dashboard for a page of notifications that carries no sort parameter, or an option in Frontend's sort select that is not an ordering. src/server/app/services/persistence/records/real/lifecycle/read.js:26 and :34 default the parameter and always send it, and the four options at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/dashboard/copy/copy.en.js:27-36 are all orderings.

increments.title: Choosing a sort order on the dashboard does nothing until the trader also presses "Update sort"; Design release 1 shows the select with no button beside it
increments.detail:
A secondary button labelled "Update sort" sits immediately to the right of the sort select and submits the form that carries it (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/dashboard/template.njk:63-82). Changing the select alone re-orders nothing; the trader has to change it and then press the button. The same pattern applies to the filter panel, whose "Search" button is the only way to apply the keyword.

Design release 1's toolbar holds the results count and the sort select and nothing else (app/views/dashboard.html:231-251). There is no button beside the select and none anywhere in the filter panel, so on the face of the design a choice takes effect on its own.

This finding may be wrong, and the reason it is banded disputed is that Design release 1 gives no evidence its select works at all. The prototype's dashboard route reads a sort query parameter but never applies it: getDashboardViewModel (app/routes.js:7138-7255) passes the value to the select so the right option shows as chosen and into the pagination links, and orders the notification list nowhere. Nothing on the page submits the form the select sits in either — there is no button, and the prototype ships no dashboard script that submits on change, none of the twenty-one files in app/assets/javascripts mentioning the sort control. So Design release 1's sort control changes nothing whichever way it is driven, and the absent button could equally be a design decision to apply on change or an unimplemented corner of a prototype. Settle it before doing anything: if it is a design decision, the frontend should submit the form when the select changes and drop the "Update sort" button from src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/dashboard/template.njk:63-82, with a no-JavaScript fallback that keeps the button visible. If it is prototype incompleteness, the frontend is already right and this finding is struck.

FALSIFIED BY: A Design release 1 dashboard capture in which changing the "Sort by" select re-orders the list without any further action by the user.

If it is prototype incompleteness, the frontend is already right and this finding is struck.
finding.correction: The banding and the settling question are right and are kept. One sentence in the difference slot was factually wrong and has been fixed: it said "the prototype's dashboard route does read a sort query parameter and apply it". It reads it and does not apply it. getDashboardViewModel builds its visible list by tab, filter and page slice only, and the entire file contains just two .sort( calls, one on address names and one on a label list, neither reachable from the dashboard. That makes the case for disputing stronger rather than weaker — Design release 1's select demonstrably re-orders nothing at all, so its missing button is no evidence either way about apply-on-change. The toolbar citation was also a few lines short — it started at the select's label rather than at the <form> that holds the count and the select — and now reads app/views/dashboard.html:231-251, which is the whole toolbar the sentence describes.
finding.falsifiedBy: A Design release 1 dashboard capture in which changing the "Sort by" select re-orders the list without any further action by the user.
finding.verification: Ran the falsifier as far as it can be run from a static corpus and then went to the source, which settles it more cheaply. dr1-dashboard.html contains exactly one <form> — the results toolbar holding the sort select — and its only <button> elements are the service-navigation toggle and the two MoJ date pickers' own controls, so there is no submit anywhere near the select and the filter inputs are not even inside a form. Read app/views/dashboard.html:230-251 and src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/dashboard/template.njk:63-82. Listed app/assets/javascripts: 21 files, and the 5 that contain the string "sort" are all search widgets (country, commodity, airport, transit-country, address-book-lookup) sorting their own result arrays; none touches the dashboard. Opened evidence/prototype@491b3926/page/dr1-dashboard.png (select alone, no button) and evidence/frontend@76a864ba/page/fe-dashboard-populated.png ("Update sort" immediately right of the select). The disputed banding survives.

relatedTo.why: Same control; one is what the options say and the other is how the choice is applied.

decision.note: Deferred by Sam, 2026-08-21: the dashboard is temporary, so no sort work for now. This was the run's disputed finding about whether Design release 1's sort applies on change or needs an Update button — its select sits in a GET form with no submit control and no script to submit it, so the pipeline refused to state it as fact. The deferral settles it without anyone having to answer that question.

increments.title: The dashboard's sort control names a field and a direction in four options; Design release 1 names what the trader wants in three — newest first, oldest first, arrival date
increments.detail:
The list is headed by a "Sort by" select offering four orderings: "Arrival (newest to oldest)", "Arrival (oldest to newest)", "Date created (newest to oldest)" and "Date created (oldest to newest)" (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/dashboard/copy/copy.en.js:27-36, assembled at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/dashboard/view-model/sort-options.js:8-18). Arrival newest-first is selected when the page loads and there is no unsorted option, so the trader cannot see the list in whatever order the service returns it.

Design release 1's select is labelled "Sort by:" and offers "Select one", "Newest first", "Oldest first" and "Arrival date", in that order and taken from app/data/dashboard-notifications.js:147-152, rendered at app/views/dashboard.html:238-250. "Select one" is what the page loads with, so the design's starting state is an unsorted list and no ordering is named until the trader chooses one. The design names what the trader wants — the newest notifications, the oldest, or the next to arrive — rather than naming a field and a direction.

Replace the four options in src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/dashboard/copy/copy.en.js:27-36 with the design's three plus an unselected "Select one", and relabel the control "Sort by:". "Newest first" and "Oldest first" map onto the existing createdAt directions and "Arrival date" onto arrivalDate, so src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/dashboard/view-model/sort-options.js:8-18 and the sort parser it feeds change with them. This is copy and the labels behind it, and it lands entirely in Frontend against the design as it already stands, so the band is frontend-work and nothing has to come first. What "Select one" means for the list query — that the page can load with no ordering applied at all, which Frontend has no state for — is a behaviour change rather than copy and is raised on its own as service-wide--dashboard-loads-with-an-ordering-already-applied. The three named orderings here can be relabelled without it, and it can be built without them.

increments.title: The dashboard's button to begin a notification reads "Start a new notification" and is a GOV.UK start button; Design release 1 uses a standard button reading "Create a new notification"
increments.detail:
The dashboard shows a green start button reading "Start a new notification" with the chevron icon, rendered with isStartButton (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/dashboard/template.njk:30-33, text from src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/dashboard/copy/copy.en.js:7). It is the tallest thing on the page and is the pattern GOV.UK reserves for the entry point to a whole service.

Design release 1 shows a standard button reading "Create a new notification" directly under the heading (app/views/dashboard.html:32-36). It carries no start-button icon and no extra height, so it reads as one action among several on a signed-in landing page rather than as the front door to the service.

Change the label to "Create a new notification" in src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/dashboard/copy/copy.en.js:7 and drop isStartButton from the call at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/dashboard/template.njk:30-33 so it renders as a standard button. The form around it stays: the frontend creates the notification with a POST and Design release 1 uses a link, which is an implementation difference and not part of this change.

FALSIFIED BY: Finding a govuk-button--start class or the words "Start a new notification" on the captured dr1-dashboard screen.

increments.title: Frontend shows no phase banner; Design release 1 carries an Alpha banner with a feedback link on every page
increments.detail:
No page in the service carries a phase banner. The shared layout builds the GOV.UK header, the service navigation, the signed-in bar and the breadcrumbs, and goes straight into the page content with nothing between (src/server/app/shared/layout.njk:19-53). There is no govukPhaseBanner import and no phase-banner markup anywhere in src/server, and none of the 67 captured frontend screens renders one. So a user is never told the service is in Alpha and is never offered a way to give feedback.

Every one of the 60 captured Design release 1 screens opens with a phase banner directly under the service navigation: a grey "Alpha" tag followed by "This is a new service. Help us improve it and give your feedback by email.", with "give your feedback by email" as a link (app/views/dashboard.html:15-20). Each view declares it in its own beforeContent block rather than in the layout, so the banner is repeated per view but is present on all of them.

Render a govukPhaseBanner in the shared layout's beforeContent block, above the breadcrumbs and back link, so it appears on every page including the dashboard: tag text "Alpha", body "This is a new service. Help us improve it and give your feedback by email." with the last five words as a link. The banner text belongs in src/server/app/shared/copy.en.js beside the existing layout copy at :10-21. Design release 1 points the feedback link at a placeholder, so this service needs a real destination — a feedback form or a mailto address — decided before the work lands; the banner itself does not depend on it.

FALSIFIED BY: Finding phase-banner markup in the captured DOM of any frontend screen, or a Design release 1 root view whose beforeContent block omits the banner.

increments.title: The documents page and the consignment addresses hub end with a button reading "Continue"; Design release 1 reads "Save and continue" on both, and reads "Continue" only on check your answers and the declaration
increments.detail:
Almost every journey page ends with a primary button reading "Save and continue", which is what the shared button macro renders when a page passes no primary of its own (src/server/app/shared/save-actions.njk:5, reading src/server/app/shared/copy.en.js:43). Four pages pass their own primary and label it just "Continue", and between them they account for twelve of the sixty-seven captured frontend screens: the accompanying-documents page in all four of its captured states (fe-documents, fe-documents-populated, fe-documents-scanning, fe-documents-error), the consignment addresses hub in all three (fe-addresses-hub, fe-addresses-hub-empty, fe-addresses-hub-complete), check your answers in all three (fe-check-answers, fe-check-answers-incomplete, fe-check-answers-submitted) and the declaration in both (fe-declaration, fe-declaration-error). The two overrides that matter are src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/template.njk:92 and src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/template.njk:16, each reading a per-feature copy key set to the string "Continue" at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/copy/copy.en.js:51 and src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/copy/copy.en.js:8. On both of those pages the "Continue" button sits immediately to the left of a secondary button reading "Save and return to hub", so the page offers the user a choice between a button that says it saves and a button that does not.

Design release 1 ends the same two pages with "Save and continue". Upload documents states it at app/views/upload-documents.html:245 and the consignment addresses hub at app/views/roles-and-addresses.html:114, and both render it beside a secondary "Save and return to overview". Design release 1 does use a bare "Continue" — but only on two pages, and they are the two at the end of the journey where there is nothing left to save: review your notification (app/views/review-notification.html:184) and the declaration (app/views/declaration.html:91), each of which ends with that single button and no secondary. Across the sixty captured Design release 1 screens the primary reads "Save and continue" on forty-five and "Continue" on seven, and those seven are review notification and its incomplete state, the declaration and its error state, add a transporter, the contact address for the consignment, and add an address to the address book.

Change the two per-feature copy keys from "Continue" to "Save and continue": src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/copy/copy.en.js:51 and src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/copy/copy.en.js:8. The documents override must stay in place because it also carries name="action" and value="continue", which the post dispatcher branches on; only its text changes. The addresses override carries nothing else, so that page can drop its primary argument at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/template.njk:16 and fall through to the macro's default instead. Seven captured screens change: the four documents states and the three addresses hub states. FIVE MUST NOT CHANGE. Check your answers and the declaration already read "Continue" on both sides, because Design release 1 reads "Continue" there too — so fe-check-answers, fe-check-answers-incomplete, fe-check-answers-submitted, fe-declaration and fe-declaration-error are already right and renaming them would introduce a difference that does not exist today. This is not a service-wide rename; it is two copy keys. Two boundaries with neighbouring findings, because a corpus-wide duplicate sweep has already run and this is a new near-neighbour. First: service-wide--save-and-cancel-buttons-name-the-hub renames the two controls to the RIGHT of this button — "Save and return to hub" and "Cancel and return to hub" — which come from the shared keys at src/server/app/shared/copy.en.js:42-45 and change on every page at once. This finding is the button to their left, which comes from each page's own copy and changes on two pages. Different strings, different files, different blast radius. Second: documents--continue-discards-a-filled-in-document says that pressing this button on the documents page throws away a document the trader has filled in but not added. These two must land together or the copy one must land second, because renaming the button to "Save and continue" while it still discards makes the label state something untrue. One further difference runs the other way and is already recorded elsewhere: on two pages Design release 1 reads "Continue" where the frontend reads "Save and continue" — the contact address page and the transporter-type page — and that is inside service-wide--save-and-cancel-shown-where-the-design-shows-one-button, whose own screens are those pages and whose change removes the surrounding controls at the same time. It is deliberately not folded in here.

FALSIFIED BY: Finding a primary submit button whose text is exactly "Save and continue" in the captured DOM of dr1-upload-documents or dr1-roles-and-addresses, or one whose text is exactly "Continue" in the captured DOM of fe-documents or fe-addresses-hub — either would mean the two sides agree on the pages this finding says they disagree on.

finding.verification: Author and verifier are the same agent on this one, and it had no independent verifier — say so when reading it. It was raised after a pre-ingest editor met the difference while correcting a false sentence inside service-wide--save-and-cancel-buttons-name-the-hub, judged it out of that finding's scope, and asked for it to be written up on its own. Every count below was re-derived here from the captured DOM rather than taken from the editor, and they agree. Extracted the text of every submit button in all sixty-seven captured frontend files and all sixty captured Design release 1 files, then tallied the labels: the frontend renders "Save and continue" thirty-nine times, "Save and return to hub" forty-one times and "Continue" twelve times; Design release 1 renders "Save and continue" forty-five times, "Save and return to overview" twenty-nine times and "Continue" seven times. Listed the twelve frontend files holding a bare "Continue" and they are the four documents states, the three addresses hub states, the three check-answers states and the two declaration states — four pages, not twelve. Listed the seven Design release 1 files holding a bare "Continue" and they are review notification and its incomplete state, the declaration and its error state, dr1-transporter-add, dr1-contact-address-for-consignment and dr1-address-book-add. Traced the frontend labels to source — src/server/app/shared/save-actions.njk:5 renders the macro's default only when a page passes no primary, and the two pages that pass one read src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/copy/copy.en.js:51 and src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/copy/copy.en.js:8 — and the Design release 1 labels to their root views, which are app/views/upload-documents.html:245, app/views/roles-and-addresses.html:114, app/views/review-notification.html:184 and app/views/declaration.html:91, none of them under a release subfolder. Opened evidence/frontend@76a864ba/page/fe-addresses-hub.png, which shows the three controls in order: a green "Continue", a grey "Save and return to hub" and a "Cancel and return to hub" link. On the documents page this button today discards a document the trader has filled in but not added, so relabelling it "Save and continue" before that behaviour changes would make the label state something untrue.

Line 114 is the primary text alone, so the secondary was outside the range. 113-125 holds both buttons in the same actions block: Save and continue at 113-118 with name=action value=continue, and the secondary Save and return to overview at 120-125. This is a widen within the template that genuinely holds both strings, not a repoint of a rendered-page quote.

increments.title: The save and cancel controls at the foot of every journey page send the user back to "the hub"; Design release 1 calls the same page the overview
increments.detail:
Every journey page ends with the same three controls, built by one shared macro (src/server/app/shared/save-actions.njk:3-13): a primary "Save and continue" button, a secondary "Save and return to hub" button and a "Cancel and return to hub" link. The wording comes from src/server/app/shared/copy.en.js:42-45. Both strings appear on 41 of the 67 captured frontend screens. The page they name is headed "Overview", so the word "hub" appears nowhere the user can see it except on these two controls — it is the internal name for the task list.

Design release 1 uses the same three-control pattern with the same primary label, and names the destination after what it is headed: "Save and return to overview" and "Cancel and return to overview" (app/views/consignment-details.html:145). Both strings appear on 29 of the 60 captured screens.

Rename saveAndReturnToHub to "Save and return to overview" and cancelAndReturnToHub to "Cancel and return to overview" in src/server/app/shared/copy.en.js:42-45. Both keys are read only by src/server/app/shared/save-actions.njk:3-13, so one edit changes every page. The three controls and their order do not move, and the key names themselves can stay as they are; only the strings are user-visible. The primary button beside them, however, does not always agree, and this rename does not touch it: on seven captured frontend screens the primary reads "Continue" where the Design release 1 screen it pairs with reads "Save and continue" — the three consignment-addresses hub states (fe-addresses-hub, -empty and -complete, against dr1-roles-and-addresses and dr1-roles-and-addresses-answered) and the four documents states (fe-documents, -populated, -scanning and -error, against the dr1-upload-documents family). It is not a blanket difference: on check-your-answers and on the declaration both sides read "Continue", so the two designs agree there. That primary label does not come from src/server/app/shared/copy.en.js:42-45 and is not read by src/server/app/shared/save-actions.njk:3-13 — each of those pages passes its own — so it is a different edit in different files and it is recorded here as an observation rather than folded into this rename.

FALSIFIED BY: Finding the word "hub" in a button or link label in the captured DOM of any Design release 1 screen, or "overview" in one on the frontend side.

finding.correction: The copy claim is correct and the slot is unchanged, but the prototype slot's opening — "Design release 1 uses the same three-control pattern" — is true only of the 29 screens that carry it. Comparing the two sets against pairs.cjs, five frontend page groups render the secondary button and the cancel link where the Design release 1 page they pair with shows a single primary button and no cancel: origin, cph-number, contact address, transporter type against dr1-transporter-add, and private transporter. That is a difference in whether the pattern appears at all rather than in what it says, so it is recorded as its own finding, service-wide--save-and-cancel-shown-where-the-design-shows-one-button, and this one is left to the wording alone. A SECOND CORRECTION, MADE BY THE CORPUS EDITOR IN A PRE-INGEST EDIT PASS AND NOT BY THE VERIFIER ABOVE. What was claimed: the difference slot ended "Nothing else about the pattern moves — the three controls, their order and 'Save and continue' already agree." What is true: the primary button's label does not always agree. On seven captured frontend screens it reads "Continue" where the Design release 1 screen it pairs with reads "Save and continue". How it was checked: grepped the captured frontend DOM for a button label of exactly "Continue" and got twelve files — the three consignment-addresses hub states, the four documents states, the three check-your-answers states and the two declaration states. Read the primary button out of each one's paired Design release 1 capture, taking the pairs from pairs.cjs rather than guessing them. capture/html/frontend/fe-addresses-hub.html:198-203 renders "Continue" as the primary with "Save and return to hub" beneath it, while its pair capture/html/prototype/dr1-roles-and-addresses.html:346-361 renders "Save and continue", "Save and return to overview" and "Cancel and return to overview" — so the two secondary controls this finding renames sit under a primary that already disagrees. fe-addresses-hub-complete.html:200 and fe-addresses-hub-empty.html:189 are the same. The four documents states pair with the dr1-upload-documents family, whose primary is "Save and continue" at capture/html/prototype/dr1-upload-documents.html:541. The other five of the twelve are not differences: dr1-review-notification.html:1142 and dr1-declaration.html:320 both read "Continue", matching the frontend's check-your-answers and declaration pages. Why the verifier missed it: the counter-examples are all on screens belonging to other slices, and this finding's own screens are fe-consignment-details and dr1-consignment-details, where the primary does agree. The difference slot now states the seven screens and says explicitly that the primary label is out of scope of this rename, because it comes from each page's own copy rather than from the shared keys this finding changes. The rename itself is untouched and still correct.

increments.title: Five journey pages end with a save-and-return button and a cancel link that Design release 1 does not show there, where the design ends the page with one button
increments.detail:
Every journey page that renders the shared save-actions macro gets all three of its controls, because the macro takes no argument that would drop one (src/server/app/shared/save-actions.njk:3-13): a primary "Save and continue", a secondary "Save and return to hub" and a "Cancel and return to hub" link. The two return controls appear together on 41 of the 67 captured frontend screens, and on every screen where either appears the other does too. So a user meets the same three-way choice at the foot of the origin page, the CPH number page, the contact-address page, the transporter-type page and the private-transporter page.

Design release 1 shows the three-control pattern on 29 of its 60 captured screens and ends the other journey pages with a single button. On five pages that pair with frontend pages carrying the full set it shows one control and no way to leave: origin-of-the-import, cph-number and transporter-add-private end with "Save and continue" alone — the origin page's whole form-actions block is one button at app/views/origin-of-the-import.html:167-175 — and contact-address-for-consignment and transporter-add end with a button reading just "Continue". The private-transporter page is the one exception with a second control, and it is a third destination rather than the overview — a "Cancel and return to dashboard" link.

Stop rendering the secondary button and the cancel link on the five pages the design ends with one button, and leave the pattern intact on the pages that keep it. The macro at src/server/app/shared/save-actions.njk:3-13 renders all three unconditionally, so it needs a way to ask for the primary alone — a flag on the macro, read by the five feature templates — rather than five copies of a shortened button group. Two of the five also differ in the primary label, "Continue" against "Save and continue", and one carries a cancel link to the dashboard rather than the overview; those are copy on individual pages and belong with whoever picks up this change, not with the shared macro. Design release 1 states no rule for which pages carry the full pattern, so the design's own list is the specification: the five named here lose it and the rest keep it.

increments.title: Frontend shows no section caption above the page heading, so a user cannot tell which part of the notification they are in; Design release 1 captions almost every page
increments.detail:
Journey pages open straight into the h1 with nothing above it — the origin page renders {{ copy.title }} as a bare heading (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/origin/template.njk:10), and so does every other journey template. Only the five party pickers caption their heading, with "Consignment addresses" (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/party-picker/party-picker.njk:7, text from src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/copy/copy.en.js:42). Nine of the 67 captured frontend screens carry a caption and all nine are party pickers. The dashboard carries none.

45 of Design release 1's 60 captured screens print a caption above the heading naming the part of the notification the page belongs to. Seven captions are used across the journey — "About the consignment", "Consignment parties", "Transport and arrival", "Movement", "Documents", "Commodity details" and "Add a new transporter" — and the first six match the hub's own section names, so a user working through a section always knows which one they are in. The origin page reads "About the consignment" above "Origin of the import" (app/views/origin-of-the-import.html:38-40). The dashboard is captioned "Dashboard" above the service name (app/views/dashboard.html:28-30), and the address-book add page "Add a new address". Fifteen captured screens go uncaptioned: the overview and the review page in both their states, the submitted page, the declaration in both its states, the contact address for the consignment, and seven of the eight address-book screens.

Add a caption above the h1 on every journey page the design captions, taking its text from the hub section the page belongs to, and add "Dashboard" above the dashboard heading. The section name is already known to the flow — the hub builds the same grouping at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/flow/task-rows.js:27-59 — so this is a layout change plus one string per section rather than a per-page decision. Where the frontend already captions a page it uses the wrong words: the five party pickers say "Consignment addresses" where the design says "Consignment parties", so src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/copy/copy.en.js:42 changes with the rest. Leave uncaptioned the pages the design leaves uncaptioned: the overview, the confirmation, the check-answers page, the declaration and the contact address for the consignment.

increments.title: Frontend's service navigation carries no items; Design release 1 offers Dashboard, Address book, Manage account and Log out on every page
increments.detail:
The service navigation bar holds the service name and nothing else — src/server/app/shared/layout.njk:27-32 calls govukServiceNavigation with serviceName and serviceUrl and passes no navigation array, so the bar renders as a single link reading "Import notification service". Below it a separate right-aligned strip shows the signed-in user's email address and a "Sign out" link (src/server/common/components/service-header/template.njk:9-29). "Manage account" and "Address book" appear nowhere in the service: neither string occurs in any of the 67 captured frontend screens. So from any page there is no way to reach the dashboard, the address book or an account page other than by using the browser or the service-name link.

The item matching the current page is marked active and rendered with aria-current, so on the dashboard "Dashboard" is underlined. There is no separate signed-in strip and the user's identity is not shown; sign-out lives in the navigation as "Log out".

Pass a navigation array to govukServiceNavigation in src/server/app/shared/layout.njk:27-32 with the four items, and set the active item per page so the current section is marked. Move sign-out out of the bespoke strip at src/server/common/components/service-header/template.njk:9-29 and into the navigation as "Log out", which leaves that strip carrying the user's email alone — decide whether it stays at all, since Design release 1 shows no signed-in identity. Two of the four items need a destination this service does not yet have: "Address book" points at the address-book UI being built in trade-imports-ins-frontend, and "Manage account" has no owner named anywhere. Add the items with real hrefs where they exist and agreed placeholders where they do not — Design release 1 itself points both at a placeholder. Whether the address book belongs to this service is a separate question, recorded under address-book--saved-address-book-pages-absent.

increments.title: On the first page of a new notification the frontend shows neither its status nor its reference; Design release 1 shows both from that page onwards
increments.detail:
Every journey page opens with a status strip — a coloured tag and the notification's reference in bold (src/server/app/shared/layout.njk:65-70) — and 56 of the 67 captured screens show one. The origin page is the exception. Its controller only passes the journey to the strip once an answer has been committed (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/origin/controller.js:88-89 and :107, using hasCommittedNotificationAnswers from src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/flow/entry-guard.js:37), so on the first page of a brand-new notification the strip is absent and the user is not told either that the notification is a draft or what its reference is. All three captured origin screens show the gap, and the reference does exist by then: it is the journey id already in the page's own URL and in its breadcrumb links.

Design release 1 prints the strip on the origin page from the first visit — a blue "Draft" tag and the notification reference beside it, rendered by the shared partial at app/views/partials/notification-status.html:18-24 and included by the page before its caption. The design carries it on 45 of its 60 captured screens and drops it only outside a notification in progress: the dashboard, the eight address-book screens, the declaration in both its states, the submitted page and the two transporter-add screens.

Show the status strip on the origin page for a new notification as well as a resumed one, by passing the journey to kit.base unconditionally at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/origin/controller.js:107 instead of through journeyIfStarted at :88-89. Nothing else has to change: the strip's tag and reference already come from src/server/app/shared/kit.js:53-58, which needs only the journey, and the journey exists on that request because the same controller uses its id for the back link and the breadcrumbs. The separate decision the same helper drives — where the origin page's Back link points before an answer is saved — is not touched by this.

increments.title: Frontend's arrival date hint spells out the earliest and latest date the user may enter; Design release 1's hint gives a worked example of the date format instead
increments.detail:
Under "Arrival date at port of entry" the hint reads "The expected date of arrival at the port of entry. Enter a date between {earliest} and {latest}." — the second sentence names both ends of the accepted window, computed from today (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/transport/copy/copy.en.js:6-7, filled in at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/transport/port-of-entry/port-of-entry.controller.js:97-101). It shows the user the boundaries but never shows them what a date should look like.

Under the same label the hint reads "The expected date of arrival at the port of entry. For example, 27/3/2026" (app/views/partials/arrival-date-picker.html:13). The second sentence is a worked example of the format, not a range, and it does not move.

Replace the second sentence of the arrival date hint with a worked example of the date format. The dates inside the two sentences are not what differs — both services derive the same seven-days-back, six-months-forward window from the clock, and both drive the date picker's bounds from it, so the window itself is unchanged. What differs is what the sentence is for: Design release 1 tells the user how to write a date, the frontend tells them which dates are allowed. Whether the range should still be stated anywhere is a copy decision that follows from adopting Design release 1's wording; the date picker already refuses out-of-range days and the frontend already has an out-of-range error message for the typed case (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/transport/copy/copy.en.js:34-35).

increments.title: The button that opens the arrival date calendar is a grey box with a dark icon; Design release 1 draws it as a blue button with a white icon

increments.title: A Frontend user whose commercial transporter is not one of the two on the list has no way to record it; Design release 1 lets them add one, giving its authorisation number, name, address and contact details
increments.detail:
The commercial branch is select-only. The page is a radio group and nothing else: two transporters, a Save and continue button, a Save and return to hub button and a Cancel link (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/transport/transporters-select/transporters-select.njk:11-23). There is no add link, no add button and no add route — nothing in src/server matches a transporter add path — and the validator rejects any answer that is not one of the listed ids (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/transport/transporters-select/transporters-select.controller.js:22-28). The private branch is not an escape either: it collects a name, an address and contact details but no transporter authorisation number, so it cannot stand in for a commercial transporter. A user whose commercial transporter is not one of the two is left with no way to record it. They are not stopped — they can go back to the type question and declare the same firm as a private transporter, typing its name and address by hand — but the notification then carries the wrong transporter type and no approval number at all.

The transporter list carries an "Add a transporter" button under it (app/views/transporter.html:162-163). It leads to the type chooser, and choosing Commercial leads to a form headed "Add commercial transporter" under the caption "Add a new transporter". The form opens with a notification banner headed "Help with transporter authorisation" repeating the DAERA and APHA rules, then asks for: Transporter authorisation number; Name or organisation name; Address line 1; Address line 2 (optional); Town or city; County (optional); Postcode or Zip code; Country, which is fixed to Northern Ireland and cannot be changed; then, under a sub-heading "Enter contact details", Email address and Phone number hinted "For international numbers include the country code". The type chooser states the same restriction in words: Commercial is hinted "This can only be a commercial transporter from Northern Ireland." The added transporter joins the list and can then be selected.

Add a page that lets a user enter a commercial transporter that is not on the list, reached from the transporter list rather than from the type question. It asks for a transporter authorisation number first, then name, the six address fields, a country locked to Northern Ireland, and an email address and phone number. The Northern Ireland restriction is a rule Design release 1 states twice and it has to be carried into the page and into the type chooser's hint. The frontend already stores a chosen commercial transporter as a name, an address and an approval number (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/transport/transporters-select/transporters-select.controller.js:75-81), so a hand-entered one fits the answer shape that already exists and no contract outside the frontend has to change. increments.title: Opening the arrival date calendar drops it on top of the next two questions; Design release 1 opens it in the flow of the page so nothing is covered
increments.detail:
The calendar floats. It is positioned over the page and the rest of the form stays where it was, so the open dialog lands across "Port of entry" and "Means of transport to the port of entry": in the captured screenshot the port hint is sliced in half by the calendar's edge, the port field is hidden behind it, and only the tail of one "Vessel" radio shows below. A trader who opens the calendar to check a date can no longer see the two questions they were about to answer, and has to close it to get them back. The frontend takes the Ministry of Justice date picker exactly as the package ships it — `src/client/stylesheets/application.scss:2` imports the component's own stylesheet and adds nothing, and the page calls the macro unadorned at `src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/transport/port-of-entry/port-of-entry.njk:16` — and that component's default is an overlay.

Design release 1 opens the same calendar in the flow of the page. It sits directly under the date field and pushes "Port of entry", "Means of transport to the port of entry" and everything after them down the page, so nothing is ever covered and the whole form stays readable with the calendar open. This is deliberate and Design release 1 says so about itself in a comment on the rule that does it — "MOJ date picker — in-flow calendar (pushes content down, no overlay)" — before pinning the dialog to `position: static` with a fixed maximum width (app/assets/sass/application.scss:18-31, applied to the arrival page's date field at :1663-1665). A small script clears the inline offsets the component writes each time the dialog opens, so the layout holds.

Take the arrival date picker's dialog out of overlay positioning on the port-of-entry page: give it static position, full width up to a fixed maximum, and a small top margin, so opening it pushes the following questions down instead of covering them. The frontend has no stylesheet of its own for this component yet — `src/client/stylesheets/application.scss:2` imports the Ministry of Justice partial and stops — so this is a new rule in the frontend's own styles rather than a change to an existing one. Note that the component writes an inline `top` when it opens (the captured dialog carries `style="top: 43px;"`), so the rule has to beat that inline value or the offset has to be cleared when the dialog opens, which is what Design release 1 does. The crop for this finding is the date field itself; the evidence for the covering is in the two whole-page screenshots, which is where the difference is visible.

increments.title: Frontend asks for the transit countries as one long checkbox list of every eligible country; Design release 1 has the user search for a country at a time and builds a table of the chosen ones, each with a Remove link
increments.detail:
Below the same heading and the same two explanatory sentences, the page is a single checkbox fieldset legended "Select all countries the consignment will travel through", hinted "Select up to 12 countries", with one small checkbox per country running down the page (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/transport/transit-countries/transit-countries.njk:16-23). There is no way to search it, and once countries are ticked the only record of the choice is the ticks themselves, scattered down the list in alphabetical position — the page never gathers them together and there is nothing to remove a country with other than finding its box again.

Below the identical heading and identical two sentences, the page asks one country at a time. A field labelled "Enter a country", hinted "Enter each country that the consignment will travel through", holds a search box placeholdered "Search for a country" with a magnifier button; picking a match adds that country and clears the box. The chosen countries then appear beneath, under a "Country" header, one per row, each with its own "Remove" link — in the captured state, France and Germany with a Remove beside each (app/views/transit-countries.html:58-136). Everything the user has chosen is visible in one short list they can act on.

Replace the transit-countries checkbox fieldset with a search-and-add control and a summary of what has been chosen. The user needs a search field labelled "Enter a country", hinted "Enter each country that the consignment will travel through", that matches against the country list and adds the picked country; and, under it, a list of the chosen countries headed "Country" with a Remove link on each row. The upper limit does not change — both services cap the selection at twelve — but the way it is communicated does, because Design release 1 has no room for a standing "Select up to 12 countries" hint and announces the limit only when the user reaches it. Design release 1 also announces each addition to assistive technology as it happens, so the new control needs a live region rather than only a visible row.

increments.title: Frontend refuses to leave the transit countries page until at least one country is chosen; Design release 1 treats the list as optional and lets a road or rail consignment through with none
increments.detail:
The question is compulsory once it applies. `transitedCountries` is in scope and mandatory whenever the means of transport is rail or a road vehicle (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/transport.js:92-105), so a trader who presses Save and continue without ticking a box gets the page back with "There is a problem" and the message "Select at least one country the consignment will travel through", both in the error summary and above the checkbox list (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/transport/copy/copy.en.js:55). The notification cannot be submitted until a country is chosen, because the transit-countries task row has to be fulfilled like every other in-scope row.

Design release 1 asks the same question of the same traders and accepts no answer to it. Its transit-countries handler runs no validation of any kind: it clears any errors, saves whatever was posted — including an empty list — and moves on (app/routes.js:10533-10537). Its completeness check for the section is a function that returns a literal true with the comment "Transit countries are optional — any saved list (including empty) is acceptable" (app/routes.js:1932-1935), and the section is absent from the ten predicates that gate submission. So a road or rail consignment reaches the declaration with no transit country recorded, and nothing anywhere tells the trader one was expected.

Make the transit-countries answer optional. In src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/transport.js:92-105 the in-scope branch keeps `inScope: true` and its reason but drops `status: 'mandatory'`, so the question is still asked of rail and road consignments and still purged for the others, but an empty selection no longer holds the task row out of fulfilled and no longer blocks submission. The "Select at least one country the consignment will travel through" message then has nothing to fire on and goes with it, along with the error state of the page. Nothing has to land first — the obligation and its copy are both frontend files, and the notification contract already carries an empty list. Note that this is a change to whether the question must be answered, not to how it is asked: replacing the checkbox list with a search-and-add control is transport--transit-countries-is-a-checkbox-list, and that work should carry this rule rather than the current one.

FALSIFIED BY: A validation error on Design release 1's transit-countries page after pressing Save and continue with no country chosen. Design release 1's captured page could only be photographed in its unanswered and answered states, so this is the one observation that would settle it, and the handler at app/routes.js:10533-10537 has no branch that could produce one.

Split the transport identification hint into a lead-in sentence and a four-item bulleted list, keeping the wording of the items exactly as it is. increments.title: Frontend's transporter authorisation guidance sends the user to a different GOV.UK page from the one Design release 1 sends them to, and words two of its lines differently
increments.detail:
The transporter authorisation guidance opens the transporter type page: the lead sentence about DAERA and APHA, three bullets, a guidance link, and two closing sentences. The link reads "Find out how to transport animals in connection with an economic activity (opens in new tab)" and goes to https://www.gov.uk/guidance/transporting-animals-in-great-britain, which is the general page on transporting animals in Great Britain. The last sentence reads "Documents issued in any EU Member State are not valid for use in GB." The whole block is one copy object at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/transport/copy/copy.en.js:62-77, rendered at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/transport/transporters/transporters.njk:8-18.

Design release 1 shows the same guidance, in the same order, at the top of its transporter page (app/views/transporter.html:48-62). The lead sentence and all three bullets match the frontend word for word. Two lines do not. The link reads "…(opens in a new tab)" and goes to the animal-welfare-in-transport guidance, anchored at its section on transporting animals in connection with an economic activity — a different page, and one that lands the user on the specific section rather than at the top of a general one. The last sentence reads "Documents issued in any EU member state are not valid for use in GB.", in sentence case.

Bring the transporter authorisation guidance block into line with Design release 1: point the guidance link at https://www.gov.uk/guidance/animal-welfare-in-transport#transporting-animals-in-connection-with-an-economic-activity, change its text to end "(opens in a new tab)", and lower-case "member state" in the closing sentence. All three strings sit in the one guidance object at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/transport/copy/copy.en.js:62-77, so this is a single edit to a single block rather than three scattered ones. Take the href from Design release 1 without the Google Analytics linker parameters its prototype copy carries — those are an artefact of how the URL was pasted, not part of the requirement. Where the block ends up on the page is settled by the flow change raised beside this one, which moves the guidance onto the transporter list; this finding is only about what it says.

FALSIFIED BY: Finding the frontend's guidance link pointing at the animal-welfare-in-transport page, or Design release 1's pointing at transporting-animals-in-great-britain, in the two captured rendered DOMs.

increments.detail:
Each transporter is one radio. Its label is the transporter's name and its hint is a single sentence built by joining the address lines with commas and appending the approval number after an em dash — "43 East Hague Extension, Delectus sitodio p. Laborum Odio tempor, Quasoccaecat ut ear, 30055, Switzerland — approval number ES-T2-45001294" (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/transport/copy/copy.en.js:92-93, built at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/transport/transporters-select/transporters-select.controller.js:55-65). Status is a coloured tag: a green "Approved" on six of the eight rows and a pink "New" on Romanian Agri Exports SRL and Finnish Livestock Oy, which tells a user at a glance that a transporter has been added but not yet approved.

Render the transporter list as a table with a radio per row and columns for Name, Address, Approval number, Type and Status, and show the approval status as a tag. Type only carries meaning once the list holds both commercial and private transporters, so schedule this after the flow change that combines them. Design release 1's "View details" link opens the transporter as an address-book record; whether the frontend has anywhere for that link to go is the address-book slice's question, not this one, so build the columns and leave the link out until that is settled.

increments.title: Frontend asks which type of transporter is moving the animals before showing any list; Design release 1 shows one searchable list of all approved transporters, commercial and private together, and asks the type only when a user adds a new one
increments.detail:
The transporter section opens on a page that begins with the DAERA and APHA authorisation guidance and only then asks the question. Below that guidance sits the heading "What type of transporter will move the animals?", hinted "We will ask for the transporter's details next.", with two radios, Commercial ("A business approved to transport animals — you will choose one from a list") and Private ("You or another individual moving the animals — you will give their address"). The answer forks the journey: Commercial goes to a list of approved commercial transporters to pick one from, Private goes to a blank name-and-address form. The two branches never meet, so a user whose transporter is already known to the service but is a private one has no list to pick it from and types the whole address again. The order and the fork are declared as three consecutive pages in one section at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/flow/flow.js:67-76, and the copy at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/transport/copy/copy.en.js:60-61.

The transporter section opens on one page headed "Transporter details", introduced "This is the person or company responsible for transporting the consignment.", carrying the same DAERA and APHA guidance apart from the wording and destination of its guidance link, then "Select a transporter" over a searchable table of every transporter the trader can use. The table mixes both kinds: Yusen Logistics (Romania) SRL, Roadtrain Ltd, Danish Meat Export ApS and Portuguese Livestock Lda are typed Commercial, and Aberdeen Livestock Ltd, Romanian Agri Exports SRL, Slovak Farm Export and Finnish Livestock Oy are typed Private. A user picks a row and continues. Only a user who cannot find their transporter presses "Add a transporter", and only then is the type question asked, on a separate page headed "Choose a transporter type" warned "Before you add this transporter, please ensure you have already searched for it first." (app/views/transporter-add.html:32-36). The linear journey holds one transporter step, /transporter (app/routes.js:1274); both add pages sit off it.

Restructure the transporter section so the list comes first and the type question comes second. The frontend needs one transporter page that lists every transporter available to the trader, commercial and private, with the DAERA and APHA guidance and the "This is the person or company responsible for transporting the consignment" introduction on it, and a route off that page for adding one that is not listed. The type chooser then moves off the linear journey onto that add route, asked only of a trader who could not find their transporter in the list, and the two branches it forks into become the two ways of adding a transporter rather than the two ways of choosing one. The words on the chooser and on the private form it leads to also change, and that is raised separately as transport--transporter-type-chooser-copy-differs so it can land on the pages as they stand today without waiting for this. This is the parent of four other transport findings and should land before them: the list needs a search box, the list needs Type and Status per row, the add route needs a commercial form, and the chooser needs Design release 1's copy. Nothing outside the frontend has to change first — the list is a local fixture at src/server/app/services/commercial-transporters/records.js:7-29 and it can be widened to carry private transporters there.

FALSIFIED BY: Finding a route in the frontend that reaches a combined transporter list before the type question is asked, or finding that Design release 1's /transporter table filters to one type once a transporter type has been chosen.
